triage.notes: 本記事は2004-2024年の81研究をまとめたレビュー論文であり、特定の発生事例やアウトブレイクの報告ではない。結核は既知の慢性感染症であり、ケア遅延の要因分析は公衆衛生研究として重要だが、EBSのシグナルトリアージ対象外と判断。

article.articleHeadline: 我国科学家揭开斯氏按蚊更能传播疟疾的秘密
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chinese scientists uncover the secret behind Anopheles stephensi's greater ability to transmit malaria.
article.articleSummary: Anopheles stephensi, a heat-tolerant, city-adapted malaria mosquito, is expanding from South Asia and the Middle East into Africa, heightening urban malaria risk amid warming climates. A joint team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Shanghai Normal University identified a key mechanism: a 5-kb deletion in the timeless (tim) circadian gene that becomes enriched under elevated temperatures. In high-temperature conditions, homozygous tim deletions disrupt mating, while heterozygous males gain a 3.6–4.7-fold mating advantage, promoting rapid frequency increase. The mutation stabilizes the clock in heterozygotes, boosting energy use and pheromone production, increasing female attraction. However, tim-deletion-bearing females show reduced resistance to the malaria parasite; infection rates rise from 74% to 97.5% and parasite load increases, enhancing transmission. The results, published online in Cell on November 20, 2026, link circadian genetics to heat adaptation and malaria transmission, informing vector control under climate change.

triage.headline_ja: 中国の科学者、ハマダラカ(スティーブンシ)がマラリアをより伝播しやすい秘密を解明
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は中国の研究機関による基礎科学研究（蚊の遺伝子メカニズム解明）の報告であり、実際の感染症発生イベントではないため、トリアージ対象外。
triage.notes: 本記事は中国の研究チームによる基礎研究成果の発表であり、具体的な感染症発生事例の報告ではない。研究内容はアフリカ等におけるマラリア媒介蚊の気候適応に関するものだが、現地での発生状況を報告するものではないため、対象国として特定国を列挙しない。

article.articleHeadline: Metagenomic Sequencing Detects Severe Legionnaires' Disease in
article.articleSummary: Legionella pneumophila pneumonia in 54 hematological patients in China was identified by metagenomic next-generation sequencing followed by PCR confirmation, across cohorts from the Institute of Hematology & Blood Diseases Hospital (CAMS & PUMC) and Tianjin Union Precision Medical Diagnostic. More than half (51.9%) developed severe Legionnaires' disease, with 28‑day mortality 35.2% overall and 67.9% (19/28) among severe cases. Fever was universal; cough 92.6%; expectoration 79.6%; dyspnea 64.8%. Radiology showed mass-like consolidation in 61.1%, often mimicking invasive fungal pneumonia; polymicrobial infections occurred in 61.1%. Only 13.0% (7 patients) had empiric anti‑Legionella therapy before pathogen identification. Multivariable analysis associated higher CRP (HR 1.106 per 10 mg/L) and higher metagenomic sequencing read counts (HR 2.645 per tenfold increase) with increased 28‑day mortality. Authors conclude mNGS enables rapid recognition in hematology patients and highlight need for validation of predictive markers.

triage.headline_ja: メタゲノム解析により血液疾患脆弱患者における重症レジオネラ症を検出
triage.triage_reason: 特定の血液疾患患者コホートにおける後ろ向き臨床研究であり、公衆衛生上のアウトブレイクやヒト-ヒト感染拡大の懸念を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は中国天津の血液疾患専門病院における臨床研究論文の紹介であり、レジオネラ症はヒト-ヒト感染せず環境曝露由来の日和見感染であるため、公衆衛生緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: 我国科学家揭示疟蚊耐热奥秘
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chinese scientists unveil the secret of Anopheles mosquitoes' heat tolerance.
article.articleSummary: Malaria vector Anopheles stephensi in urban settings shows enhanced heat tolerance linked to a natural deletion in the timeless (tim) clock gene, tim⁻⁵ᵏᵇ. Conducted by teams from the CAS Center for Excellence in Molecular Plant Science and Shanghai Normal University in Shanghai, China, the study reared mosquitoes at 32°C day/30°C night for ~80 generations and compared to a 27°C control, with population genome sequencing revealing tim⁻⁵ᵏᵇ. This deletion rises from 2.08% in normal-temp populations to 28.65% after high-temperature selection. The mutation stabilizes the circadian clock in heterozygous males at high temperature, increasing mating competitiveness and allowing rapid spread. Females carrying tim⁻⁵ᵏᵇ exhibit weakened anti-malarial immunity, boosting infection rates from 74% to 97.5% and increasing parasitic oocysts and sporozoites, thereby enhancing malaria transmission. Findings illuminate a molecular mechanism linking circadian gene variation to heat adaptation and malaria risk, informing population monitoring, risk assessment, and targeted control. Published November 20, 2026; Cell.

triage.headline_ja: 中国科学者がマラリア蚊の耐熱メカニズムを解明
triage.triage_reason: 蚊の適応進化に関する基礎研究であり、直接的な感染症アウトブレイクではない。ただし、都市部マラリアベクトルの耐熱性上昇と感染能力増強は将来のリスク要因として注視の価値あり。
triage.notes: 本記事は学術論文公表（Cell誌、2026年11月20日）に関する科学ニュース。現在のアウトブレイク報告ではなく、マラリアベクター（Anopheles stephensi）の耐熱性獲得メカニズムに関する基礎研究。都市部での蚊の適応進化と感染能力向上は中長期的なマラリア拡大リスク要因として関心を持つべき。ただし即座の公衆衛生脅威を示す情報（患者発生、流行報告）は含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Cholera cases in Philippines rise 69 pct in two weeks
article.articleSummary: Cholera cases in the Philippines rose 69% over a two-week monitoring period, with 27 cases recorded from Oct 11–24, up from 16 in the prior two weeks; cumulative cholera cases total 551, 61% lower than a year earlier, according to the Department of Health (DOH). The DOH urged the public to drink safe water and thoroughly cook food amid El Niño conditions. In the same period, typhoid fever cases rose 4% to 1,141, and influenza-like illness increased 8% to 15,925. Dengue cases reached 254,090 from Jan 4 to Nov 7, down 9% year-on-year. Location: Philippines. Publication date: 2026-11-20.

triage.headline_ja: フィリピンのコレラ症例、2週間で69%増加
triage.triage_reason: コレラ症例数は2週間で69%増加したが絶対数は少なく(27例)、累積では前年比61%減少しているため深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威とは言えない。El Niño下での水系感染症のルーチン監視報告であり、継続的な動向観察が妥当。
triage.notes: DOHによる定期的な感染症サーベイランス報告。コレラ、腸チフス、インフルエンザ様疾患、デング熱の複数疾患の動向データを含むルーチンレポート。死亡者数等の重症度情報は記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue Congress Reviews Highlight Vaccine Efficacy and Integrated Vector
article.articleSummary: Dengue vaccines and integrated vector-control strategies dominated 2025 infectious-disease congress discussions. Brazil’s 2024 outbreak totaled about six million dengue cases and ~6,000 deaths, with individuals over 60 accounting for roughly two-thirds of fatalities; chronic diabetes and hypertension, plus heterologous infections, heighten risk of severe disease. Dengue virus, a Flaviviridae member transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, is spreading into non-endemic regions, including parts of North America and Europe. Three licensed live-attenuated vaccines were reviewed: CYD-TDV (yellow fever backbone) requires serostatus screening and has been discontinued due to safety concerns in seronegatives; TAK-003 (two-dose) showed 61% efficacy against symptomatic dengue and 84% against hospitalization in DEN-301 over up to 4.5 years, with a booster achieving 74% and 90% in later follow-up; Butantan-DV (single-dose) demonstrated 77% overall efficacy over five years. Real-world data from Mexico City, the United States, and São Paulo (2024 outbreak driven by serotypes 1 and 2) supported durability and serotype-balanced responses across age groups.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱会議レビュー:ワクチン有効性と統合ベクター管理戦略
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は学会でのデング熱ワクチン有効性レビューであり、2024年ブラジル流行は過去データとして引用されているのみで、新規の急性公衆衛生事象ではない。
triage.notes: 記事は2025年の学会レビューであり、ブラジルの2024年デング熱流行（約600万症例、約6000人死亡）は過去の統計データとしてワクチン有効性議論の文脈で引用されている。新規イベントのシグナルとしては該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Mutirões contra dengue retiram 605 toneladas em Pato Branco
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue-control campaigns remove 605 tonnes in Pato Branco
article.articleSummary: Pato Branco, Brazil, reports dengue-control campaigns have removed about 605 tonnes of discarded materials since July across three neighborhoods, aiming to curb Aedes aegypti breeding. The November Rapid Indices Survey for Aedes aegypti found larvae in 0.4% of inspected properties, highlighting ongoing risk of dengue, Zika and chikungunya transmission. Endemic-control teams recorded 100,682 visits from July 1 to November 17, inspecting homes, businesses and other sites. Mass cleanup efforts yielded: Alvorada—515 tonnes across 103 loads (Sept 28–Oct 15); Menino Deus—60 tonnes in 12 loads (Nov 9–11); Alto da Glória with Vila São Pedro and São João—30 tonnes in six loads (Nov 16–18). In October, 26 CMEIs (Municipal Centers for Early Childhood Education) lectures educated on preventing Aedes proliferation. Community participation remains essential: eliminate containers and other materials that collect water.

article.articleHeadline: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan dedicates India's first indigenous bird flu vaccine by ICAR-NIHSAD to nation
article.articleSummary: India unveils its first indigenous H5N1 avian influenza vaccine, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, dedicated in New Delhi to the nation on November 20, 2026. The vaccine aims to safeguard poultry against highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks that have afflicted India since 2006, including more than 500 outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes and causing heavy losses from culling, trade restrictions, and farm deaths. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan framed the milestone as a step toward Atmanirbhar Bharat, noting the vaccine could halt transmission from poultry to humans and reduce economic damage. A BSL-4 laboratory will be established at NIHSAD in Bhopal to support ongoing research and containment. HPAI remains a serious disease in birds with up to 100% mortality in affected flocks; the vaccine represents a critical tool for poultry sector resilience.

article.articleHeadline: Haut-Uélé /Ebola : à Isiro, des prestataires du centre de traitement annoncent une grève
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Haut-Uélé / Ebola: In Isiro, treatment center staff announce a strike.
article.articleSummary: Isiro's Ebola Treatment Center at the General Reference Hospital in Haut-Uélé faces an imminent work stoppage as frontline staff threaten a dry strike starting November 21, 2026. The action follows four months of unpaid premiums (August–November 2026) amid repeated security incidents at the facility. After a November 19 meeting, staff warned they will resume only once all due premiums are paid and that any suspension could hinder ongoing Ebola response. They also highlighted vandalism at the center, including theft of a staff phone, destruction of the morgue, and removal of a dead body, emphasizing unsafe working conditions. The protest comes as the province already reports Ebola cases in Wamba territory, Watsa, and the city of Isiro, underscoring ongoing outbreak pressure and concerns for containment.

triage.headline_ja: オート・ウエレ州/エボラ出血熱：イシロの治療センター職員がストライキを予告

triage.notes: 記事は治療センター職員の労働争議が主題だが、背景として同州内（ワンバ、ワツァ、イシロ）でのエボラ症例継続が明記されており、アウトブレイク対応への悪影響が懸念される。国際的拡大や渡航制限に関する情報は本記事には記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: अब मुर्गियों को नहीं होगा बर्ड फ्लू? भारत ने बनाई पहली स्वदेशी वैक्सीन
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Will chickens no longer get avian influenza? India has developed the first indigenous vaccine.
article.articleSummary: On 20 November 2026, India launched its first indigenous H5N1 avian influenza vaccine for chickens, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, targeting the H5N1 clade 2.3.2.1a strain. The vaccine aims to curb outbreaks and reduce culling losses in poultry. From 2006–2021, India reported 341 bird-flu cases across 24 states, including 284 H5N1 and 57 H5N8 infections. Experts say vaccination can lower human risk by reducing infection in poultry and environmental viral load, but it will not fully eradicate the disease; continued farm hygiene, surveillance, and safe disposal of infected birds remain essential. While H5N1 can infect humans via contact with infected birds, there is no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission. Properly cooked chicken and eggs remain safe; risk is highest during handling of infected birds.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola vaccine trials launches amid security concerns
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola strain outbreak in DR Congo's east has killed over 5,500 people and caused more than 11,000 cases since May, with the epicenter in conflict-torn Ituri and North Kivu. Large-scale trials launched for three vaccines targeting Bundibugyo: Tumaini (at least 1,000 participants to assess safety and efficacy); Ervebo, Merck's Zaire-strain vaccine, began on Oct. 23; two additional candidates from Oxford University and Moderna will join soon. If data show safety and effectiveness, regulators will still review before emergency-use authorization, potentially enabling expanded access; deployment could occur in early to mid-2027. Trials face severe security and misinformation challenges amid ongoing fighting with rebel groups including M23, with health workers attacked and thousands displaced, complicating enrollment. WHO reports 400–500 new weekly cases and notes delays paying frontline responders.

triage.headline_ja: 治安上の懸念の中、エボラワクチン治験が開始
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部でブンディブギョ株によるエボラ流行が5月以降死者5,500人超・症例11,000件超に達し、週400〜500件の新規症例が続く深刻な事態であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準とも複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 紛争地域（イトゥリ州、北キブ州）での流行であり、M23等の武装勢力による治安悪化が対応や治験参加者募集を妨げている。WHOは前線対応者への支払い遅延も報告しており、管理能力の課題が大きい。

article.articleHeadline: Mycoplasma Pneumoniae Surged While RSV Declined in Hospitalized Children in
article.articleSummary: Two-year molecular surveillance of 604 pediatric hospitalizations for acute lower respiratory infections in northern China (Hebei Children's Hospital, Shijiazhuang) shows Mycoplasma pneumoniae dominance rising from 32.4% in 2023 to 54.3% in 2024, while RSV fell from 21.4% to 7.3% and influenza A from 9.7% to 1.3%. Across 601 complete multiplex panels, at least one pathogen was detected in 528 cases (87.9%), with M. pneumoniae identified in 261 episodes (43.4%). Age-standardized analyses indicate M. pneumoniae increased to 52.1% in 2024 from 35.5% in 2023, whereas RSV declined to 8.0% and influenza A to 1.3%. After adjusting for age, sex, and month, 2024 remained associated with higher odds of M. pneumoniae detection (adjusted OR 3.09, 95% CI 1.94–4.94). Median age rose from 3.0 to 5.0 years; deep-airway secretions underwent 13-pathogen multiplex PCR testing.

triage.headline_ja: 中国北部の入院小児においてマイコプラズマ肺炎が急増、RSVは減少
triage.triage_reason: 中国河北省における小児呼吸器感染症の2年間の分子疫学サーベイランス研究であり、マイコプラズマ肺炎の増加は近年世界的に報告されている既知の現象で緊急性は低いが、小児における流行性病原体の継続的動向として注視する価値がある。
triage.notes: 本記事は学術研究の報告であり、過去2年間（2023-2024年）の後方視的サーベイランスデータに基づく。新規の公衆衛生緊急事態を示すものではなく、既知のマイコプラズマ肺炎流行パターンの疫学的記録である。重症度（死亡率等）の詳細は記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Cholera cases in Philippines rise 69 pct in two weeks
article.articleSummary: Cholera cases in the Philippines rose 69% during Oct. 11–24, reaching 27 cases, up from 16 in the preceding two weeks, according to the Department of Health (DOH). Cumulative cholera cases stand at 551, about 61% lower than a year earlier. The DOH urged the public to drink safe water and thoroughly cook food amid El Niño conditions that can elevate water and food contamination risks. No deaths are reported in the update. The data reflect ongoing national monitoring of cholera activity, with risk communication emphasizing hygiene, safe water and proper cooking as key prevention measures as El Niño persists. Public health authorities continue monitoring for potential spread and advise on water safety.

triage.triage_reason: 直近2週間で症例数が69%増加したが、死亡例はなく累計症例数も前年同期より61%少ないため、重大な公衆衛生上の脅威とは言えないが、エルニーニョによる水・食品汚染リスクの継続を踏まえ今後の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Scientists are learning more about the rare Ebola virus in Congo outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has infected over 11,000 people and caused more than 5,500 deaths in a six-plus month span, with transmission primarily when patients are symptomatic. Bleeding is uncommon (5-10%), complicating differentiation from malaria and delaying diagnosis; about 70% of fatalities occur in the community rather than in health facilities. Children under five account for 1,207 confirmed cases and 844 deaths (~70% fatality in this group), higher than adults (about 50%). Declared in May 2026, sequencing shows Bundibugyo is not rapidly changing or more transmissible. There are no licensed vaccines or treatments yet; Merck's Ervebo is being tested for cross-protection, while Bundibugyo-specific vaccines and antivirals from Gilead/Mapp are entering trials. Emphasized: enhanced care improves survival and standard control measures like isolation remain effective.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴの希少なエボラウイルス流行について、科学者たちが知見を深めている
triage.triage_reason: DRCでの希少なブンディブギョ型エボラ流行は11,000人以上が感染し5,500人以上が死亡する大規模・重症な事例であり、ワクチン・治療薬未確立で国際支援が必要なためフルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断した。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC東部での希少なブンディブギョ型エボラ流行の規模と重症度（特に5歳未満児の致死率約70%）を詳述。ワクチン・抗ウイルス薬は治験段階であり、国際的な研究・支援が進行中。

article.articleHeadline: Los científicos avanzan en el conocimiento de la rara variante del ébola en el brote del Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists Make Progress in Understanding the Rare Ebola Variant in the Congo Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is contending with the Bundibugyo Ebola variant in a protracted outbreak now over six months. By 2026-11-20, authorities report more than 11,000 cases and over 5,500 deaths, with Bundibugyo transmission faster than the West Africa 2014–2016 outbreak. There are no approved treatments or vaccines. The surge unfolds amid a severe humanitarian crisis; common symptoms include fever, vomiting and diarrhea, while hemorrhages occur in only 5–10% of confirmed Bundibugyo infections. Diagnosis is delayed because Bundibugyo is not detected by tests for other species and can resemble malaria. In children under 5, 1,207 cases and 844 deaths (about 70% fatality). Genomic sequencing shows the virus is not mutating rapidly or more transmissible. Outbreak was formally declared in May; transmission may have begun months earlier. About 700 recoveries are in follow-up studies.

triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ・ブンディブギョ株が6ヶ月以上流行し1万人超の感染・5500人超の死亡という深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、承認された治療薬・ワクチンがなく国際的拡大・支援の必要性も高いため。
triage.notes: 承認された治療薬・ワクチンがなく、5歳未満児の致死率約70%と極めて深刻。診断の遅延やマラリアとの類似症状も懸念材料。フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Gli scienziati stanno acquisendo nuove conoscenze sul raro virus Ebola nell'epidemia in Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists are gaining new insights into the rare Ebola virus in the Congo outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus is driving the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak, with over 11,000 cases and more than 5,500 deaths as of 2026-11-20. The rare Bundibugyo variant is spreading at about twice the rate of West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic, and there are no approved treatments or vaccines. Researchers in eastern Congo, a region already affected by a humanitarian crisis, caution that data are limited and difficult to compare across outbreaks. Hemorrhagic symptoms occur in only about 5–10% of confirmed cases, fewer than the Zaire variant, complicating diagnosis and contributing to many deaths at home (around 70%). The outbreak was declared in May, but transmission may have begun months earlier. Among children under five, 1,207 cases and 844 deaths (~70% mortality); adults ~50% mortality. Genomic sequencing shows no rapid viral change or increased transmissibility; about 700 survivors are in follow-up studies.

triage.headline_ja: 科学者たちはコンゴのエボラ出血熱流行で稀なエボラウイルスに関する新たな知見を得ている
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で稀なブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスが流行し、11,000例超・死者5,500人超と深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、承認された治療薬・ワクチンが存在せず、西アフリカ2014-2016年流行の約2倍の速度で拡大している異常事態のため、フルリスク評価に進むべきと判断。
triage.notes: Bluedotの発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではコンゴ民主共和国（特に東部地域）のみが言及されており、Angolaへの言及はないため除外した。出血性症状は確定例の5-10%のみで診断が複雑化し、在宅死亡率が約70%に達している点、5歳未満児の致死率が約70%である点も深刻度を示す重要な情報。

article.articleHeadline: Čínská mobilizace proti africkému moru prasat | Náš chov - vše o chovu hospodářských zvířat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chinese mobilization against African swine fever | Our Farm - All About Livestock
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) in China began with the first confirmed outbreak on August 3, 2018 in Shenyang, Liaoning. In the ensuing weeks, four outbreaks led to the culling of more than 25,000 pigs. By 2019 ASF was detected across nearly the entire country and in several East and Southeast Asian countries. Genetic analysis confirms the Georgia 2007 lineage; the introduction route remains unproven, but movement of live pigs or pork products is the most plausible pathway. The epidemic caused about a 30% reduction in sows and roughly a 40% drop in pork production, lifting prices and increasing imports. China responded with a three-year disease-control and production-recovery plan, shifting from fragmented to more centralized pork production and strengthening biosecurity. No functional ASF vaccine exists; prevention relies on stringent on-farm biosecurity, including entry testing, isolation, rigorous sanitation, material decontamination, and comprehensive vehicle and facility decontamination involving heat, UV, ozone, and fumigation.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ豚熱に対する中国の動員対応について | Náš chov（家畜飼育情報サイト）
triage.triage_reason: 2018年発生のアフリカ豚熱（ASF）に関する歴史的・解説的記事であり、新規の感染症発生イベントを報じるものではない。ASFは動物疾患でヒトへの健康影響もないため、公衆衛生上の新規シグナルには該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は2018年8月に瀋陽で始まったASF流行とその後の中国の防疫対策を振り返る歴史的・畜産業向け解説記事であり、新規発生や現在進行中のアウトブレイクを報じるものではない。ASFはヒトに感染しない動物疾患であり、IHR(2005)の対象となる公衆衛生事象には該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola killed 46 members of one man's family. Now he is fighting to save the rest
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Bunia, Ituri province. In six months, more than 11,000 cases confirmed and nearly 5,400 deaths, with authorities cautioning figures may be higher; children account for over a third of deaths. The Bundibugyo virus carries a roughly 50% fatality rate; there is no specific treatment or approved vaccine yet, though clinical trials are ongoing per the WHO. The article recounts Birungi Nembe and her mother Sylvie Bongerize Tibasima: Sylvie was diagnosed at birth and died a week later; Birungi contracted Ebola and died by early September. Cases have been confirmed in Kenya and Nigeria. Transmission linked to funerals and contact with bodies; distrust and insecurity hinder containment. Bunia hosts more than 1 million displaced people amid ongoing violence, with 80+ attacks on health workers and 400–500 new weekly cases, though some areas show declining infections.

triage.headline_ja: エボラがある男性の家族46人の命を奪った。彼は残りの家族を救うために闘っている

triage.notes: 記事中でケニア・ナイジェリアでの症例確認が言及されているが、両国は本トリアージの対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外した。治安悪化・医療従事者への攻撃・国内避難民100万人超という状況が封じ込めを著しく困難にしている点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Les scientifiques en apprennent davantage sur le rare virus Ebola dans l'épidémie qui sévit au Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists are learning more about the rare Ebola virus in the outbreak ravaging the Congo.
article.articleSummary: In the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Bundibugyo form of Ebola has caused over 11,000 confirmed cases and more than 5,500 deaths since the outbreak began in May. Transmission is about twice as fast as the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic, and there is no approved treatment or vaccine. Hemorrhages occur in roughly 5–10% of confirmed Bundibugyo cases, making the illness harder to distinguish from malaria and delaying diagnosis, as Bundibugyo-specific tests were not always available. About 70% of deaths occur in the community rather than in health facilities. Children under five account for 1,207 confirmed cases and 844 deaths (~70% mortality in this group), higher than adults (~50%) but lower than Zaïre and other Ebola strains. Genomic sequencing shows Bundibugyo mutates slowly and is not more transmissible; questions remain on mild symptoms and long-term outcomes. WHO and Africa CDC urge cautious interpretation of limited, heterogeneous data.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで猛威を振るうエボラ流行、希少なウイルスについて科学者らが理解を深める
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行は11,000例超・5,500人以上の死亡という深刻な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、IHR基準の複数（深刻性、異常性、国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーはコンゴ民主共和国東部での流行のみを扱っており、Angolaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。マラリアとの鑑別困難による診断遅延が指摘されており、二次的な公衆衛生リスクも懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Wetenschappers krijgen meer inzicht in zeldzame ebolavariant tijdens uitbraak in Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists gain more insight into a rare Ebola variant during an outbreak in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus is driving an outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with more than 11,000 infections and over 5,500 deaths after six months. The Bundibugyo variant spreads twice as fast as the West Africa 2014–2016 outbreak, yet there are no approved treatments or vaccines. The eastern Congo setting, already in humanitarian crisis, complicates data collection, and authorities warn against premature conclusions. Symptoms include fever, vomiting, and diarrhea; bleeding occurs in only about 5–10% of confirmed Bundibugyo cases, complicating diagnosis and enabling misdiagnosis as malaria. About 70% of patients die at home rather than in care centers. Among children under 5, 1,207 cases and 844 deaths (roughly 70% mortality) have been reported; adult fatality is ~50%. Genomic sequencing shows the virus isn’t rapidly changing, but questions remain about mild cases and long-term effects. Isolation and standard public-health measures appear to help, and transmission seems linked to symptomatic cases.

triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではコンゴ東部のみが言及されており、Angolaでの発生は確認できないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: 我国科学家揭示疟蚊耐热奥秘 -泉州网|泉州晚报社 泉州新闻门户网站
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chinese scientists reveal the secret of malaria mosquitoes' heat tolerance.
article.articleSummary: Malaria, one of the world's deadliest mosquito-borne diseases, is increasingly shaped by climate warming as Anopheles stephensi expands into urban areas. In China, researchers from the CAS Center for Excellence in Molecular Plant Science and Shanghai Normal University (Liu Jingnan's team) studied heat adaptation by rearing An. stephensi at 32°C day/30°C night for ~80 generations, versus a 27°C control. Genome analyses revealed a natural 5 kb deletion in the timeless circadian clock gene tim (tim-5kb, tim⁻⁵kb); its frequency rose from 2.08% in normal temperatures to 28.65% after high-temperature selection. The tim-5kb mutation maintains clock stability in hybrid males, boosting mating competitiveness under heat and driving allele spread. It also weakens female anti-malarial immunity, increasing infected females from 74% to 97.5%, and elevating oocyst and sporozoite counts, thereby enhancing malaria transmission. Published in Cell on November 20, 2026, these findings inform climate-driven adaptive evolution, surveillance, and targeted control strategies.

triage.headline_ja: 中国の科学者がマラリア蚊の耐熱性の秘密を解明

triage.notes: この記事は中国の研究機関による基礎研究報告であり、実際のマラリア患者の発生や流行を報じたものではない。ただし、記載内容は気候変動に伴うマラリアベクター（ハマダラカ）の耐熱性獲得と病原体伝播能の増強に関する科学的知見を示唆している。将来の流行リスク評価には関連性があるが、現時点では緊急的なシグナルではない。公式な感染症イベント（患者発生・流行）の情報が今後得られた際の参考資料としての価値がある。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever: Mandaue wants to inspect private lot near school
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-20, Mandaue City, Cebu reported 15 dengue-positive individuals tied to Opao Elementary School, including two five-year-old kindergarten pupils from Opao and Umapad who died. Officials seek access to inspect a privately owned lot beside the school suspected as a mosquito breeding site; owner not yet located and security guards block entry. City Health Officers, in coordination with DepEd, plan another round of school-based mosquito-misting operations on weekends. Dengue symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, muscle and joint pains, nausea, and skin rashes. Transmission is via Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Preventive measures emphasize eliminating standing water in gutters, tires, pots, and other containers, alongside ongoing misting and clean-up drives. The city is extending financial assistance to affected families; fatalities underscore the need for stronger prevention, even as overall local cases remain lower than in other LGUs.

article.articleHeadline: El Niño pode aumentar risco de dengue no Paraná após queda de 93% nos casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: El Niño could increase the risk of dengue in Paraná after a 93% drop in cases.
article.articleSummary: Paraná, Brazil reports 6,380 confirmed dengue cases in the first 44 epidemiological weeks of 2026, 93% fewer than 2025, with six deaths. El Niño-associated heat and heavy rainfall could raise Aedes aegypti breeding and elevate transmission risk for dengue, Zika, and chikungunya, but the phenomenon is not the sole driver. The state uses 32,614 ovitraps to monitor eggs, covering about 90% of municipalities with traps every 300–400 meters in urban areas. Wolbachia-infected mosquito releases have occurred in Foz do Iguaçu, Cascavel, Londrina, Cambé, and Ponta Grossa, with Londrina beginning late October for 26 weeks. After rain, inspect yards, gutters, roofs, containers, tires and bottles; Aedes eggs resist desiccation for months and require scrubbing to remove. Prevention includes screens and ANVISA-registered repellents. A National Dengue Mobilization Day is planned for November 28 to eliminate standing water and debris, aiming to sustain control measures across municipalities.

article.articleHeadline: Rare Vibrio parahaemolyticus Strain ST859 Caused Fatal-Risk Necrotizing
article.articleSummary: Vibrio parahaemolyticus ST859 caused fulminant necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock in a 71-year-old man with alcoholic liver cirrhosis in Wenzhou, China, after handling raw seafood. Tissue culture from necrotic tissue yielded V. parahaemolyticus; ultra-multiplex sequencing detected no reads for V. vulnificus. The patient presented with septic shock, multi-organ dysfunction, rhabdomyolysis (CK up to 10,728 U/L), procalcitonin 33.98–40.07 ng/mL, platelets down to 11–36×10^9/L, and lactate 5.1–6.4 mmol/L. The isolate was susceptible to ceftazidime, cefepime, imipenem, meropenem, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, amikacin, gentamicin, TMP-SMX; resistant to ampicillin. Initial ceftriaxone failed; therapy escalated to cefoperazone/sulbactam + levofloxacin and imipenem, with fasciotomy/debridement and VAC. After stabilization, vasopressors and renal replacement therapy were weaned and the patient transferred.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bird Flu Vaccine: India's first domestically developed H5N1 vaccine prepared to protect birds from bird flu.
article.articleSummary: India launched its first domestically developed H5N1 vaccine to safeguard poultry from avian influenza. On 2026-11-20 in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, Union Agriculture Minister Shivaraj Singh Chouhan inaugurated the vaccine, developed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) at the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal. The vaccine targets the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1, clade 2.3.2.1a, marking India's first effort against H5N1. Since 2006, India has reported over 500 outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 in birds, with infection in poultry carrying up to 100% mortality. Officials expect the domestic vaccine to strengthen bird-flu prevention, reduce poultry losses, and advance India’s self-reliance in animal health as a public health measure for the poultry sector.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Indigenous vaccine dedicated to the nation for protection against avian influenza, Shivraj said—there's no need to fear anymore - Punjab Kesari
article.articleSummary: Indigenous vaccine against avian influenza (bird flu) is being developed by ICAR’s NISAD Institute in India and dedicated on 20 November, following Prime Minister Modi’s inspiration. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced via social media from New Delhi that the fully domestic vaccine will protect chickens from bird flu and, by extension, prevent human infections. The announcement notes that bird flu outbreaks in India have occurred about 500 times, and emphasizes safeguarding poultry health, farmer incomes, and rural livelihoods. The PM highlighted that indigenous vaccine development over the past 12 years has strengthened disease prevention for livestock and poultry. No laboratory confirmation details or specific outbreak data beyond the 500-country figure are provided in the report. The effort aims to shield both animals and people from avian influenza outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: Denúncias contra dentista por transmissão intencional de doença chegam a seis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Complaints against a dentist for intentional transmission of disease have reached six.
article.articleSummary: Six women in Rondônia, Brazil, have accused dentist Jean José Dunga, 41, of intentionally transmitting HIV through intimate relationships; investigations span multiple cases, with some already leading to an August conviction and new complaints under investigation. In a prior judgment, Dunga received five years and five months in a semi-open regime plus a R$50,000 indemnity, sentence appealed. He faces another criminal case with three complainants; after public disclosures, two more victims came forward. The Ministério Público de Rondônia says Civil Police investigations yielded charges of grievous bodily harm under the Maria da Penha Law, reflecting HIV as a chronic condition; penalties range two to eight years. If accepted, the latest complaints would advance to evidence and trial. Proceedings are under secrecy; Dunga was detained in September. Evidence from testimonies, medical records, and labs. HIV is managed with antiretrovirals; exposure tests and PEP within 72 hours are available via SUS.

article.articleHeadline: Analyse - Wetenschappers leren meer over zeldzaam ebolavirus in Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Analysis - Scientists are learning more about a rare Ebolavirus in Congo.
article.articleSummary: More than six months after the Ebola outbreak began in Eastern Congo, scientists are studying why the rare Bundibugyo ebolavirus spreads so rapidly. There are over 11,000 confirmed infections and more than 5,500 deaths. Bleeding occurs in only about 5-10% of Bundibugyo cases, making the disease resemble malaria and delaying recognition, as some tests initially failed to detect the variant. WHO and Africa CDC estimate transmission may have started months before the official declaration in May. About 70% of deaths occur in the community rather than in treatment centers. Children under five are heavily affected: 1,207 infections and 844 deaths (~70%). Adults’ case fatality rate is around 50%. About 700 survivors participate in research; genetic analyses show no rapid viral change or increased transmissibility. No approved Bundibugyo vaccines or treatments; Ervebo is being tested for cross-protection, with Bundibugyo-specific vaccines in development and antivirals/experimental therapies under trial in Congo.

triage.headline_ja: 分析 - 科学者らがコンゴの希少なエボラウイルスについて理解を深める
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で希少なブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスにより11,000人超の感染、5,500人超の死亡が確認されており、致死率も高く国際的な懸念が高いためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生から6ヶ月以上経過し、公式発表前から数ヶ月間伝播していた可能性がWHO/Africa CDCにより指摘されている。5歳未満の子供の死亡率が約70%と極めて高く、承認されたワクチン・治療薬が存在しない点も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola - L'ONG NRC demande "une approche plus globale et inclusive" dans la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Ebola - The NRC NGO calls for a more global and inclusive approach in the Ebola response.
article.articleSummary: May 15, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo declared its 17th Ebola outbreak, centered in Ituri amid armed conflict and 69 displaced camps. Six months on, the outbreak has killed over 5,500 people. The Bundibugyo strain driving this epidemic has no specific vaccine. Transmission occurs through contact with bodily fluids, causing hemorrhagic fever. Despite promises totalling more than $900 million, NGOs say only about one third has reached the field, with the United States as a major donor. The Norwegian Refugee Council urges a more global and inclusive response and better coordination to clarify who is intervening and which pillars are funded, to align resources with on-the-ground needs and dynamics. Emphasis is placed on strengthening community engagement to break transmission chains. This remains the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラ出血熱 - NRC（ノルウェー難民評議会）、対応における「より包括的かつ包摂的なアプローチ」を要求

article.articleHeadline: First Indigenously Developed Bird Flu Vaccine Launched: Why It Matters
article.articleSummary: India on 2026-11-20 unveiled its first indigenously developed H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from highly pathogenic avian influenza (bird flu), specifically Clade 2.3.2.1a. The vaccine, developed by ICAR-National High Security Animal Disease Institute in Anand Nagar, Bhopal, targets H5N1 and follows two decades with more than 250 outbreaks and mass poultry culling. Bird infections historically show almost 100% mortality in affected birds. Since 2006, India recorded over 500 outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8, with the 2006 outbreak causing direct and indirect losses around Rs 2,200 crore. Globally, WHO reports 1,003 human H5N1 cases with 479 deaths across 25 countries since 2003, with the Clade 2.3.2.1a strain responsible for most outbreaks in poultry and sporadic infections in mammals, including three human cases recently. The vaccine reduces outbreak risk and supports self-reliance in agriculture.

article.articleHeadline: Mpox: casos dobram no Ceará em menos de uma semana
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mpox: cases double in Ceará in less than a week.
article.articleSummary: Monkeypox cases in Ceará, Brazil doubled from 85 to 175 confirmed between Sunday, November 15, and Thursday, November 19, 2026, per IntegraSUS (State Health Secretariat). Total 448 notifications in 2026; Fortaleza hosts 145 of the confirmed cases (Caucaia 7, Sobral 4, Eusébio 3, Juazeiro do Norte 2, Maracanaú 2), with other municipalities having single cases. Fortaleza has 259 notifications, 171 discarded. In November alone, Ceará logged 358 notifications and 151 confirmed cases by Nov 19. Epidemiologist Carlos Garcia Filho notes rising transmission since late October and a possible new mpox virus strain under investigation, not yet lab-confirmed. Concentration in Fortaleza may reflect its large population and tourism. Public health measures emphasize home isolation, avoiding close contact and sharing personal items; vaccination is available for selected groups post- or pre-exposure, not for those already ill.

article.articleHeadline: Pemkot Jakpus lakukan pelacakan TBC terhadap 100 warga Petojo Utara
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Central Jakarta City Government conducts TB contact tracing on 100 North Petojo residents.
article.articleSummary: On 20 November 2026, Central Jakarta City Government conducted tuberculosis (TB) contact tracing for 100 residents in RW 05, Petojo Utara, Gambir district, as part of Kampung TBC to detect TB early and interrupt transmission. Health authorities from Gambir District Health Center and Jakarta Pusat’s Health Office performed anamnesis and screening of all residents. Individuals with prolonged cough or close contact with TB patients will undergo sputum testing to confirm TB infection. Those with close contact but no symptoms will receive TB preventive therapy (TPT) for three months, with weekly dosing. The program also offers free health checks (blood glucose, weight, height, and blood pressure). Community leaders, lurah, RW/RT, and local figures are engaged to raise awareness and promote early screening.

article.articleHeadline: India Unveils First Indigenous H5N1 Vaccine to Protect Chickens From Bird Flu
article.articleSummary: India unveils its first indigenous H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu, announced in Bhopal by Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. Developed by the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases, the vaccine targets the H5N1 virus clade 2.3.2.1a of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). Officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry said this is the first-of-its-kind vaccine produced in India, underscoring the country's self-reliance in veterinary biocontrol. HPAI remains a serious threat to poultry, with outbreaks capable of near-total mortality among infected birds. The development signals a major step in India's animal-disease defense, potentially reducing losses in the poultry sector and enhancing food security.

article.articleHeadline: Bacterial Pathogens Detected Across Urban and Peri-Urban Mammals in Greater
article.articleSummary: Across urban Legon and Madina and the peri-urban Dodowa in Ghana’s Greater Accra Region, a molecular screening of 404 mammals (185 dogs, 15 cats, 204 free-living rodents) conducted December 2019–October 2020 found widespread carriage of zoonotic bacteria. Whole-blood PCR detected genus-level Staphylococcus DNA in 293/404 animals (72.5%, 95% CI 67.8–76.8) and Non-typhoidal Salmonella DNA in 92/404 (22.8%, 95% CI 18.8–27.2). Within-host prevalence: Salmonella in cats 40.0%, dogs 22.2%, rodents 22.1%; Staphylococcus in dogs 74.1%, rodents 71.6%, cats 66.7% (cats n=15). Rodent species displayed habitat-linked patterns: Nile rat Arvicanthis niloticus predominated in urban traps; Tullberg’s soft-furred mouse Praomys tullbergi dominated peri-urban captures. DNA was amplified from 383 blood samples and 21 rectal swabs targeting ttr for Salmonella and TStaG for Staphylococcus. Findings indicate ongoing circulation of bacterial pathogens across companion animals and urban-adapted wildlife in densely populated settings.

article.articleHeadline: Why Current Ebola Outbreak Is Hard to Contain
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has infected more than 11,000 people and killed thousands, risking the largest Ebola outbreak on record. More than 5,000 deaths have occurred in DRC this month. A UK case prompted treatment at London’s Royal Free Hospital, highlighting cross-border concerns. Imperial College experts Neil Ferguson and Aula Abbara warn the outbreak will likely persist into next year and may still be spreading a year from now. Major challenges include under-detection (roughly half of cases) and two-thirds of deaths occurring in the community. Ituri and North Kivu, about the size of small European countries, suffer from conflict, poor infrastructure, malnutrition, and co-existing outbreaks. Bundibugyo virus presents non-specific early symptoms, complicating diagnosis; vaccines/monoclonal antibodies target the Zaire strain, not BVD. PPE limits care time to ~45–60 minutes, increasing heat exhaustion risk for frontline workers.

article.articleHeadline: Rare Ebola strain is hitting children hardest in devastating Congo outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola strain drives a severe outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with more than 11,000 cases and over 5,500 deaths. Among children under five, over 1,200 infections and 844 deaths yield roughly a 70% fatality rate in this group versus about 50% in adults. The eastern Congo outbreak, declared in May, is six months in and unfolds amid a humanitarian crisis, with around 70% of deaths occurring in communities rather than health facilities. Symptoms differ: fever, vomiting, and diarrhea are common, but bleeding appears in only 5–10% of confirmed cases; in young children, gastrointestinal symptoms may predominate, delaying diagnosis and treatment. Genomic sequencing shows Bundibugyo is distinct from Zaire and other Ebola strains, with no evidence of rapid change. There are no vaccines or treatments licensed for Bundibugyo; Ervebo is being tested for cross-protection, while Bundibugyo-specific vaccines and antivirals from Gilead/Mapp are in trials. About 700 survivors are in studies.

triage.headline_ja: まれなエボラ株、コンゴの壊滅的な流行で子どもを最も重く直撃
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）大規模流行で死者5,500人超、致死率も高く、国際的拡大・公衆衛生上の深刻な影響が認められるためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。

article.articleHeadline: Is Uganda Safe for Americans? Ebola, Crime and Roads
article.articleSummary: Uganda remains under a Level 4 US travel warning driven by Ebola spillover from neighboring DR Congo. The Bundibugyo Ebola strain has no approved vaccine or treatment per the CDC. DR Congo’s outbreak has 11,376 confirmed cases and 5,568 deaths as of 15 November 2026, with Ituri and Nord-Kivu at the outbreak’s center. Uganda declared its Ebola outbreak over on 28 July 2026. For travelers, Level 4 is advisory, not a ban; insurers vary. The CDC lists Uganda at Level 2 for Bundibugyo, but non-US citizens who were in Uganda in the 21 days before departure are barred from entering the United States, while returning US citizens are routed through health screening and must monitor 21 days. Uganda’s 2025 crime total was 196,405 with theft most common; road crashes 26,044 (5,383 deaths) in 2025, many involving boda-boda motorcycles. Vaccination: hepatitis A and typhoid recommended; malaria prophylaxis; yellow fever vaccination recommended, though Uganda dropped its own yellow-fever certificate rule on 2 October 2026 while CDC still lists it as required.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダはアメリカ人にとって安全か？エボラ、犯罪、道路事情

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hong Kong records two imported dengue fever cases and one imported chikungunya fever case.
article.articleSummary: Two imported dengue fever cases were reported in Hong Kong from last Friday to yesterday, with patients having travelled to Vietnam and Cambodia during the incubation period. An imported chikungunya fever case involved a 71-year-old man who had been to Mainland China during incubation. The Centre for Health Protection classifies all cases as imported infections and continues epidemiological investigations, having notified Mainland health authorities about the chikungunya case. The chikungunya patient was hospitalized in a mosquito-free environment and remains in stable condition. These reports underscore the ongoing risk of travel-associated vector-borne diseases entering Hong Kong.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, Nipah, Hendra. Ocieplenie klimatu zwiększa ryzyko zakażeń
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, Nipah, Hendra viruses. Climate warming increases the risk of infections.
article.articleSummary: BMJ-published review by University of Adelaide researchers analyzes transmission, prevention, and treatment for bat-borne viruses, including Ebola, Nipah, Hendra, Australian bat lyssavirus, and Marburg disease. The authors warn that climate warming and habitat loss disrupt ecosystems, shifting bat ranges and increasing contacts with people and domestic animals, raising spillover risk. Ebola's Bundibugyro virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda has surpassed 11,000 infections with about 50% mortality, and WHO designated it a public health emergency of international concern; fruit bats are the likely reservoir. Human infection begins from close contact with blood or secretions of infected wildlife, followed by human-to-human transmission via blood, secretions, and other fluids. Protective actions include preserving/restoring bat habitats, reducing human–bat contact, and advancing vaccines and therapies. Researchers also note eastern Australian bat die-offs linked to climate and habitat changes, and urban tree removal in Adelaide threatening roosts.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In 37 days they halted the Ebola outbreak: they wiped out the deadly virus in Kenya at record speed.
article.articleSummary: Kenya declared an Ebola outbreak contained after 37 days, with Bundibugyo ebolavirus responsible. The first case was identified October 6 in a Kenyan man returning from the region via Uganda and Congo. Nine confirmed infections were recorded in Kenya, with seven recoveries and two deaths. Four of the patients were healthcare workers. Rapid contact tracing identified 135 potential contacts; eight subsequently developed symptoms while under observation, enabling rapid isolation and preventing wider spread. The last patient was discharged by November 11, and the Kenyan surveillance period moves to a 42-day watch starting November 12; if no new cases emerge, Kenya could be declared Ebola-free on December 23. WHO notes ongoing surveillance and readiness. By mid-November, neighboring Democratic Republic of the Congo reported over 11,000 confirmed cases and more than 5,500 deaths, highlighting the danger and the value of swift response.

article.articleHeadline: Decentralized Care and Rapid Testing Support Hepatitis C Elimination in
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis C elimination by 2030 hinges on real-world delivery in LMICs, not only antiviral efficacy. WHO targets: 80% reduction in infections, 65% reduction in deaths, and diagnosis for >90% of infected people. Global chronic HCV burden: ~56.8 million. In India, viremia ~0.5% (~4.7–10.9 million). A review of 32 sources (2015–2025) identifies barriers across patient, service, technology, and policy: asymptomatic infections, limited screening, centralized NAAT, rural resource gaps, high DAA costs, blood safety issues, infection control gaps, antiviral resistance, surveillance gaps, and lack of vaccines. Scalable models favor active screening with rapid tests, decentralized care, task shifting, and telemedicine, integrated with HIV, TB, opioid substitution therapy, and prison health programs. Outcomes show cure rates similar to specialized care at lower cost; success relies on generic DAAs, point-of-care testing, stronger blood safety, resistance surveillance, and multisectoral funding and political will as of 2026-11-20.

article.articleHeadline: Fiocruz identifica novas linhagens da Covid-19 em circulação no Rio | Rio de Janeiro | O Dia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fiocruz identifies new COVID-19 lineages circulating in Rio | Rio de Janeiro | O Dia
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil sees circulation of multiple SARS-CoV-2 lineages, led by PJ.2.1, detected in 58% of 167 genomes sequenced from samples collected Oct 17–Nov 6 through Fiocruz IOC/Fiocruz and the Rio SMS collaboration. PJ.2.1 accounted for 96 genomes (58%), with RF.5 at 22% and XFG at 11%. Lineages identified in other Brazilian states (São Paulo, Espírito Santo, Distrito Federal, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina) and first detected in Canada in May, reaching Brazil in late August. WHO classifies PJ.2.1 as under monitoring. Studies suggest higher receptor ACE2 binding potentially increasing transmissibility, with moderate/low immune escape. Symptoms resemble flu or cold: fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose. Vaccination remains protective against severe disease; at-risk groups should stay up to date. Genomic data shared on GISAID and integrated into Fiocruz's Genomic Network and the Ministry of Health surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Pediatric Phase 2 Trial Shows Oral Onradivir Rapidly Suppresses Influenza A
article.articleSummary: China multicenter randomized phase 2 trial in 72 children aged 2–17 with lab-confirmed influenza A (onset within 72 hours) across 31 hospital sites evaluates oral onradivir granules (ZSP1273) given once daily for 5 days. High-dose regimens achieved target systemic exposures and rapid absorption (Tmax ~2 hours) with median Cmax 3.03–6.01 μg/mL versus 0.91–1.04 μg/mL in the low-dose arm, while tolerability remained favorable. The study, conducted November 2024–April 2025, found rapid viral clearance and maintained safety, supporting pediatric pharmacokinetic data for a novel PB2 cap-binding polymerase inhibitor distinct from neuraminidase and cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitors. Adults had prior efficacy and regulatory approval for onradivir in 2025; these results extend dosing guidance to pediatric patients for acute uncomplicated influenza A.

article.articleHeadline: Violence and mistrust hamper Ebola response
article.articleSummary: Six months after the Bundibugyo Ebola virus flare in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the outbreak remains far from contained. The situation mirrors a deadly whack-a-mole: new hotspots emerge just as early epicentres are brought under control. Violence and mistrust hamper the response, undermining contact tracing, safe burials, and health-worker access. Scores of new Ebola cases are reported across affected areas, indicating continued transmission despite public health efforts. Security challenges and community distrust complicate laboratory confirmation and the implementation of control measures. As of 2026-11-20, the DRC faces an ongoing outbreak that requires safer access, reinforced community engagement, and sustained support to halt transmission and protect frontline responders.

article.articleHeadline: Klebsiella Pneumoniae Led Confirmed Adult CNS Infections at Single Chinese
article.articleSummary: Eastern China, single hospital, 27 culture-confirmed CNS infections from Jan 2023–Apr 2026; Klebsiella pneumoniae was the most frequent pathogen, causing 7 cases (~26%). Seven non-duplicate CSF isolates underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing, whole-genome sequencing, and phylogenomics; lineage-specific core-genome SNP phylogenies were built for ST1764 and ST881. The seven isolates spanned five sequence types: ST11, ST36, ST1897, ST1764, ST881. Notably, ST11 isolates (3/7) harbored blaKPC-2 and blaCTX-M-65 and showed high carbapenem MICs. Virulence profiling revealed distinct loci across lineages; YCKP2640 (ST1764) carried iucABCD-iutA, iroBCDN, peg-344, and rmpADC; YCKP4611 (ST881) had iroBCDN, peg-344, rmpADC; YCKP4623 (ST11) harbored iucABCD-iutA, peg-344, rmpADC. Phenotypic assays showed rmpADC-positive isolates had higher capsular polysaccharide, mucoviscosity, serum survival, and greater mortality in Galleria mellonella. The string test had limited value. Conclusion: risk assessment requires integrated WGS and functional testing, as hypervirulent traits arise across diverse backgrounds.

article.articleHeadline: Pneumonia, flu spur prevention call
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-20, Minglanilla residents are urged to guard against pneumonia and influenza with respiratory symptoms in homes and workplaces, though a confirmed rise in cases has not been established. Dr. Jaclyn Mae Nadera-Cordova said medical records must be compared with prior months and last year to detect any increase. Co-workers reportedly have coughs and fever; some children recovered from coughs and colds after over-the-counter medicines. No hospitalizations for pneumonia or influenza. Influenza is a contagious viral infection of the respiratory tract; pneumonia is an infection of lung tissue by bacteria, viruses or fungi. Higher-risk groups include children under five (especially under two), adults 65+, pregnant women, and people with diabetes, heart disease or lung disease. Prevention: hand hygiene, masks when symptomatic, and influenza and pneumococcal vaccination. Those with flu-like symptoms should stay home, avoid crowds, and avoid self-medication; seek emergency care for breathing difficulties in children or severe symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Ölümcül Ebola salgınında korkunç bilanço: Tek aileden 46 kişi öldü
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Horrific toll in a deadly Ebola outbreak: 46 people from a single family died.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Bunia, has claimed about 5,400 lives among over 11,000 confirmed cases, with 400–500 new infections weekly. The World Health Organization reports a 50% case-fatality rate for Bundibugyo. No approved vaccine or specific treatment exists; clinical trials are ongoing. In Bunia, 44-year-old Sylvain Kabona Tibasima has lost 46 family members, including his sister Sylvie Bongerize Tibasima and her newborn, Birungi Nembe, who died within two weeks of birth. Burial of the infant occurred with protective gear due to transmission risk. The outbreak is worsened by armed conflict, with more than 1 million displaced and health workers subjected to 80+ attacks; despite some declines in new cases, transmission remains active.

article.articleHeadline: India unveils first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for chickens at ₹1-2 per dose
article.articleSummary: India launches its first indigenous H5N1 vaccine for chickens, priced ₹1-2 per dose, developed by ICAR’s NIHSAD in Bhopal. Unveiled by Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, the vaccine is described as the world’s first against this H5N1 variant and aims to bolster poultry disease prevention and protect farmers’ livelihoods. The NIHSAD team, led by Dr S Nagarajan, followed stringent biosafety practices, including sanitisation and high daily water use; researchers were prohibited from keeping pets. The vaccine sits within a heavy economic burden from animal diseases, with combined annual losses from FMD, Lumpy Skin Disease, Brucellosis and PPR around ₹56,000 crore. India’s bird flu history includes a 2006 Navapur outbreak that killed nearly 1 million chickens; 2021 saw ~9 lakh deaths and this year ~2 lakh. A new Bhopal lab costing ₹300 crore was announced to advance capacity.

article.articleHeadline: Actualité | Lualaba : un Fonds Sida pour ne plus laisser le virus gagner du terrain | mediacongo.net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: News | Lualaba: an AIDS Fund to prevent the virus from gaining ground | mediacongo.net
article.articleSummary: HIV/AIDS in Lualaba Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, spurs plans for a provincial AIDS Fund by the National Multisectoral Program to Fight AIDS (PNMLS). Provincial PNMLS coordinator Dr. Jacques Kwete reported over 30,000 people identified as living with HIV and on treatment, with many others likely unaware of their status and not in care. A PNMLS delegation met with the Lualaba Provincial Assembly president, Jean-Marie Kaseya, to establish the Fund to finance prevention, testing, and care for people living with HIV at the provincial level. The goal is to ensure continuity of treatment for already monitored patients and sustained access to care and antiretrovirals for new cases. Kolwezi, the provincial capital and a major hub, ranks among areas with high infection risk due to population mobility, prostitution, unprotected sex, youth vulnerability, mining expansion, and gaps in early testing and funding.

article.articleHeadline: Fatal cases of Ebola often share a striking pattern
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo's major Bundibugyo virus outbreak continues, with the CDC reporting 11,613 confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths as of November 17. Researchers studying Ebola virus find that fatal cases often have the strongest upregulation of virus-fighting genes, not shutdowns of immunity. The mechanism involves viral condensates—tiny, membrane-less droplets formed by Ebola’s NP and VP35 that accumulate 20–33% of an infected cell and trap immune messages. In human kidney cells, ~40% of messenger RNA sits inside these droplets; NP appears to drive RNA capture more than VP35. Interferon can alter droplets’ cargo, recruiting transcripts from hundreds of defense genes and making entry depend more on RNA tail shapes. With less XRN1 enzyme inside droplets, immune messages may persist longer, potentially linking vigorous immune responses to worse outcomes, as observed in fatal Ebola cases.

article.articleHeadline: Minas Gerais registra 40 cidades com surtos de sarna humana
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Minas Gerais records 40 cities with outbreaks of human scabies.
article.articleSummary: Forty municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil, report outbreaks of human scabies this year, according to the state Health Secretariat. The disease is not considered severe, but precautionary measures are essential. In Vespasiano and Lagoa Santa, schools were temporarily closed for disinfection after confirmed cases. Lagoa Santa alone has about 240 notified cases. Individuals with symptoms such as intense itching should seek medical care, and households should maintain thorough hygiene of clothing and environments to prevent spread. The report emphasizes containment through hygiene and cleaning rather than severe outcomes or fatalities, with no lab confirmation details provided. Ongoing public health management aims to curb transmission while avoiding unnecessary alarm. Date reference: 2026-11-20.

article.articleHeadline: Avian influenza scare affects chicken sales in Tiruchi
article.articleSummary: On 20 November 2026, fear of H5N1 avian influenza in Tamil Nadu’s Cuddalore district spurred a consumer scare that cut chicken sales in Tiruchi. The State government intensified surveillance and containment in affected areas. In Tiruchi, chicken availability and demand tumbled; prices fell by ₹30–₹50 per kg, while egg sales remained stable. Traders reported a sharp drop: Antony, who normally sells about 100 chickens daily, now struggles to move 20. Edamalaipatti Pudur trader H. Manickam attributed demand decline to consumer anxiety, though situation is under control. Some customers have shifted to mutton and seafood; weather conditions and fever cases also dampen purchases. Officials monitor the district; traders conduct strict quality checks on poultry before sale to reassure buyers.

article.articleHeadline: Fortaleza não tem bairros com alto risco de infestação pelo Aedes aegypti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fortaleza has no neighborhoods at high risk of infestation by Aedes aegypti.
article.articleSummary: Fortaleza, Ceará, Brazil, reports no neighborhoods at high risk for Aedes aegypti infestation after analyzing 121 bairros in the fourth LIRAa survey. The Indice Predial (IP) fell from 3.57% in the second cycle to 1.14% in the fourth, with 67 of 121 bairros presenting IP below 1%; 0 dengue fatalities were recorded during this period. Officials credit strong collaboration between the municipality and residents, reinforced by inspections by Endemias Control Agents (ACE) and Community Health Agents (ACS). Household prevention remains critical to avoid standing water and breeding sites. Measures cited include ovitramp traps, Wolbachia releases, and Larvicidal Dissemination Stations (EDLs). The Ministério da Saúde notes that temperature and rainfall shifts, intensified by El Niño, may alter mosquito circulation in Ceará. Authorities also aim to resume large-scale dengue vaccination campaigns once Butantan efforts restart.

article.articleHeadline: Maricá, Niterói e São Gonçalo 50 registram casos de Mpox
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Maricá, Niterói and São Gonçalo register 50 Mpox cases.
article.articleSummary: Mpox continues to spread in Rio de Janeiro state, with Maricá, Niterói and São Gonçalo registering 50 cases (Niterói 26; São Gonçalo 22; Maricá 2). Incidence: 5.03, 2.29 and 0.94 per 100,000 inhabitants, respectively. Across Rio, 420 confirmed cases and 1,344 notifications; 468 discarded and 448 under investigation, with one death. The capital, Rio de Janeiro city, accounts for 297 cases. In Baixada Fluminense, Nova Iguaçu has 16 cases; Duque de Caxias 11; Belford Roxo 6. Magé records 3; São João de Meriti and Queimados, 2 each; Nilópolis, Itaguaí and Seropédica each have 1. Região dos Lagos and interior also report infections. SES-RJ issued a technical note for municipal health secretaries and trained about 500 professionals (physicians and nurses) on diagnosis, patient care and prevention. The Monitora RJ dashboard provides daily updates on mpox evolution.

article.articleHeadline: Morte de jovem com Covid-19 muda entrada de presos em BH; entenda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death of a young person with COVID-19 changes inmate intake in Belo Horizonte; find out.
article.articleSummary: In Minas Gerais, Brazil, a 23-year-old detainee died after testing positive for SARS-CoV-2, prompting preventive changes in Belo Horizonte's inmate intake. The measure was adopted on 2026-11-19. The death led the Department of Penitentiary of Minas Gerais (Depen-MG) to redirect new prisoner admissions from the Ceresp Gameleira complex in Belo Horizonte to the Nelson Hungria Penitentiary Complex in Contagem, in the Metropolitan Region. The deceased was hospitalized in the public health network with pneumonia and diagnosed with an acute respiratory infection caused by the coronavirus. In a health-monitoring response, all prisoners in the gallery where the man was housed will undergo active screening to detect respiratory symptoms and potential COVID-19 or other infectious cases. The Sejusp did not disclose the gallery's occupancy, other suspected/confirmed cases, or the duration of the new intake flow. TJMG was asked for comment but had not responded as of publication.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hong Kong records two dengue fever cases and one chikungunya fever case; Centre for Health Protection says all were imported.
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong’s Centre for Health Protection reported three imported vector-borne cases from Nov 13–19: two dengue fever cases (incubation-linked travel to Vietnam and Cambodia) and one imported chikungunya case in a 71-year-old man with Mainland China travel during incubation; the patient was hospitalized in a non-mosquito environment and is stable, with the case reported to Mainland authorities. The centre said it would continue epidemiological investigations. Over the past week, four imported dengue infections and one imported chikungunya infection were recorded, involving a 44-year-old woman who travelled to the Mainland during incubation. Year-to-date dengue total stands at 40 cases, including 38 imported and 2 locally transmitted. The centre urges ongoing anti-mosquito measures in both Hong Kong and areas affected by these diseases, noting mosquitoes can still breed with autumn rain.

article.articleHeadline: Positividade de testes de covid sobe mais de 6 vezes no Brasil desde agosto
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 test positivity rate has risen more than sixfold in Brazil since August.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 test positivity in private laboratories across Brazil rose to 12.4% in late October 2026, more than sixfold since August. In epidemiological week 31 (early August), 2% of tests were positive. The five-week moving average increased from 6.4% to 8.1%, with Abramed noting no stabilization yet. Projections indicate the rate could exceed 19% in November if the trend persists, with estimates around 17% in week 45 and near 19% in week 46. The current wave lasts longer than 2025’s winter peak (16.4% at nine weeks); 2025 also had a summer peak of 28.9% in February. Guidance urges seeking medical care for shortness of breath; those with fever, cough, or sore throat should be evaluated and tested. Vaccination remains prioritized for high-risk groups (children 6 months–5 years, elderly, pregnant, immunocompromised, and those with comorbidities). Data feed to the Ministry of Health via METRICARE and RNDS.

article.articleHeadline: India develops first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, priced at ₹1-2 per dose
article.articleSummary: India launches its first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, priced ₹1-2 per dose, developed by ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (Nihsad) in Bhopal to curb poultry losses and boost disease preparedness. Since 2006, avian influenza has caused over 500 cases in India with millions of birds culled or dead; the initial outbreak was Navapur, Maharashtra (2006) with about 1 million chickens dead. In 2021 approximately 9 lakh chickens died, and about 2 lakh died in 2026. The low-cost vaccine aims to improve access for small-scale poultry farmers. India ranks second globally in egg production (149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25) and poultry exports reached 2.46 million tonnes worth $317.79 million (FY2025-26). A new ₹300 crore state-of-the-art animal disease research lab in Bhopal is announced to strengthen diagnostics. The indigenous vaccine expands Nihsad’s portfolio against highly pathogenic avian influenza, strengthening national preparedness.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Shivraj Singh Chouhan launched the first domestically produced vaccine against avian influenza.
article.articleSummary: As of 20 November 2026, India unveiled the first domestically produced vaccine against avian influenza (H5N1) for chickens, launched by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan in Bhopal. The vaccine, costing about 1–2 rupees per dose, is the world’s first H5N1 vaccine developed domestically and is aimed at safeguarding millions of poultry farmers and reducing the sector’s losses. A new high-security laboratory at ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal, costing about 300 crore rupees, was announced to support production and research. Chouhan noted this will shield livelihoods and curb the estimated annual losses from poultry diseases (foot-and-mouth disease ~₹22,000 crore; lumpy skin disease ~₹20,000 crore; brucellosis ~₹9,212 crore; PPR ~₹4,683 crore), totaling ~₹56,000 crore. Since 2006, India has faced over 500 avian influenza outbreaks, including 9 lakh bird deaths in 2021 and about 2 lakh in 2026. The vaccine marks a significant milestone in self-reliant agriculture.

article.articleHeadline: Bhopal lab develops India's first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine, single dose offers six months' protection
article.articleSummary: India's ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal announced India's first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry, targeting the 2.3.2.1a H5N1 strain. Eight scientists developed a single-dose vaccine that is expected to protect chickens for about six months. The project is pitched as a milestone for Atmanirbhar Bharat, with Union Minister Chouhan announcing a forthcoming BSL-4 lab at NIHSAD to bolster high-containment work. Bird flu, or highly pathogenic avian influenza, outbreaks have occurred in India more than 500 times since 2006, including H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes, causing mass culling and trade disruptions. Officials say the vaccine will safeguard the poultry sector and farmers' livelihoods; Chouhan stated administering it would save chickens and prevent spread to humans. This vaccine marks a key development for India's animal health sector.

article.articleHeadline: Rigorous multi-seed evaluation of domain generalization strategies for multi-center tuberculosis detection in chest radiography
article.articleSummary: TB screening on chest radiographs across four public cohorts (Shenzhen, Montgomery, TB Chest X-ray Database, GlobalSubset) with 1,280 images after de-duplication. A multi-seed leave-one-domain-out benchmark evaluated seven training objectives: ERM, MixStyle, CORAL, AdaMix (feature-mixing), IRM, GroupDRO, and HP-EAR (hyperspherical prototype entropic assignment regularizer). Each configuration trained with five seeds, totaling 140 runs, yielding 20 matched evaluations per method. Mean AUROC ranged from 0.752 to 0.767; no method differed from ERM in paired tests or mixed-effects models (p = 0.59). Rankings were unstable: three methods topped across seeds. AdaMix achieved better-calibrated probabilities (ECE 0.232 vs 0.286–0.327; Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.048). Extending training from 12 to 30 epochs did not change conclusions. At default threshold, unseen-cohort sensitivity was 0.55–0.60. Authors advocate multi-seed testing, calibration and operating-point reporting as minimum standards for domain-generalization claims in medical imaging.

article.articleHeadline: اكتشاف المزيد عن سلالة "بونديبوغيو" من فيروس إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More on the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus.
article.articleSummary: Over 11,000 Ebola cases and more than 5,500 deaths are attributed to the Bundibugyo strain in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the outbreak ongoing in eastern DRC six-plus months in. There is no approved treatment or vaccine for Bundibugyo. The outbreak is spreading roughly twice as fast as the West Africa 2014–2016 outbreak. Early conclusions are cautioned due to humanitarian crisis and limited, varied data. Symptoms include fever, vomiting, and diarrhea, but bleeding occurs in only about 5–10% of confirmed Bundibugyo cases, making diagnosis harder and more likely to be confused with malaria. Tests designed for other Ebola strains may miss Bundibugyo, contributing to under-detection; about 70% of patients die in their communities rather than in clinics. Among children under five, 1,207 confirmed cases and 844 deaths have been reported (~70% mortality). Genomic data show Bundibugyo does not mutate rapidly or become more contagious; officials expect more definitive guidance soon.

article.articleHeadline: Neue Fortschritte bei Impfungen gegen Malaria
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New advances in malaria vaccines.
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains a major burden: WHO reported about 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024, mostly in Africa, with progress stalling since 2015 amid rising drug resistance. Two vaccine approaches are reported. R21, recommended by WHO for children from five months, was tested in 54 villages in Gambia and Burkina Faso. About 60% of five‑month‑old children received three doses between May and August 2024. In The Gambia, vaccinated individuals had 3.1% parasite prevalence vs 9.5% in controls, with illnesses roughly halved across ages. In Burkina Faso, infections fell from 47.5% to 40.8%, with under-fives seeing about two-thirds fewer illnesses. Limitations include open-label design, a single malaria season, and unclear duration of protection; booster results pending; one fever convulsion noted; doses from Serum Institute. PfSPZ-LARC2 uses live, attenuated parasites with two genes deleted. In Seattle, after challenge with a Brazil-strain parasite, 2 of 15 vaccinated were infected vs 7 controls; all treated. The trial is small and not yet peer-reviewed; Burkina Faso and Tübingen trials are ongoing.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia : Solwezi Steps Up Cholera Prevention Measures
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak reported in Solwezi, North-Western Province, Zambia. Solwezi Municipal Council intensified prevention measures with chlorine sachets for domestic water treatment distributed in hotspot townships Kizhinge-Zhinge, Kazomba and Kyawama; shallow wells chlorinated (585); pit latrines lime-treated (269). Since the clean-up campaign began last month, 2,967 chlorine sachets distributed, 585 wells chlorinated, 269 latrines limed. Solid waste management in markets, bus stations, and public places enhanced; school health promotion expanded in collaboration with school managers. Information, Education and Communication materials disseminated and health education conducted to inform the public on cholera risks and prevention. Surveillance amplified and surroundings cleaned. Residents urged to maintain clean environments and good hygiene to curb transmission. The article notes no case/death counts, lab confirmation, infection source, or imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Kunci Jawaban Sejarah Kelas 11 Halaman 95, Aktivitas 2.4 Pandemi di Nusantara
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Answer Key for 11th Grade History, Page 95, Activity 2.4: Pandemic in Nusantara
article.articleSummary: Answer key for Indonesian 11th-grade History Activity 2.4 'Pandemic in Nusantara' summarizes a student exercise comparing the Spanish Flu (1918–1920) and COVID-19 (2020–2023) in Indonesia. Students form groups of 4–5 to chart similarities and differences in a table, and identify local wisdom or everyday practices as coping strategies, potentially via oral history interviews or media sources, with a class presentation of findings. The official key lists similarities: global pandemics with rapid spread across regions, social and economic disruption in Nusantara/Indonesia, and shared basic prevention such as reducing interaction, hygiene, and reliance on traditional remedies when formal medical care is limited; and government/healthcare responses to curb transmission amid limited facilities, medicines, or personnel. Differences noted: the Spanish Flu occurred under Dutch East Indies colonial rule near World War I, shaping health policy differently.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The nation's first indigenously developed vaccine made in Bhopal will protect chickens from avian influenza, with a single dose providing protection for up to six months.
article.articleSummary: On 20 November 2026, India launched its first indigenously developed avian influenza vaccine, produced by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, targeting H5N1 Indian clade 2.3.2.1a. A single-dose vaccination is reported to protect chickens for up to six months, reducing the need for frequent revaccination, with particular benefit for long-lived layer and breeder stocks. The vaccine, being domestically produced, aims to improve affordability and strengthen India’s poultry biosecurity. In India, outbreaks since 2006 have been recorded more than 500 times, causing substantial losses estimated at 2,200–3,000 crore rupees due to culling and disrupted production. While vaccines exist in China, Egypt, and Vietnam, this formulation is tailored to the Indian clade and may reduce spillover risks. The launch was announced by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.

article.articleHeadline: Brazil beat measles. The US can, too.
article.articleSummary: US now officially a measles contagion zone as PAHO announced on November 17, 2026 that the United States lost its measles-elimination status, alongside Mexico. Through 2026 the US reported more than 5,400 measles cases, over twice 2025 and about 19 times 2024; nearly all patients were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status. In contrast, Brazil has remained measles-free since 2024, recording only 70 cases in 2026, all imported—often from Peru. Brazil’s rapid response uses a 72-hour elimination ladder: report within 24 hours, investigate within 48 hours, vaccinate close contacts within 72 hours. Campaigns include Dia S door-to-door case finding and Dia D mass vaccination days; more than 16 million doses administered in 2026 and 500,000 donated to Peru. Brazil’s 2025 vaccination coverage was 76% for both doses, well short of the 95% target; US kindergarten vaccination fell to about 92%, leaving roughly 280,000 unprotected. Texas 2025 outbreak cited; political debates around vaccination persist.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルは麻疹を克服した。米国にもできるはずだ。

article.articleHeadline: [굿모닝베트남미디어] [사회/보건] 호찌민시 뎅기열 일주일 새 2,428건...직전 4주 평균 대비 25.7% 증가
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [Good Morning Vietnam Media] [Society/Public Health] Dengue fever in Ho Chi Minh City: 2,428 cases in one week, up 25.7% from the previous four-week average.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is surging in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, with 2,428 confirmed cases in the past week, up 25.7% from the four-week average; year-to-date total reaches 49,232. High-incidence areas include Con Dao Special Zone, Ngãi Giao, and Minh Thanh. Dengue, transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presents with sudden high fever, headache, muscle and joint pains, and nausea; hemorrhagic signs may occur, and severe dengue can cause plasma leakage, shock, and organ failure. Seek care for severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, lethargy, or reduced urine; avoid aspirin or ibuprofen. Prevention emphasizes removing standing water, covering storage containers, mosquito nets, and wearing long sleeves. Vaccination: Long Châu vaccine for ages 4+, two doses 3 months apart; four serotypes; reinfection risk. WHO’s TAK-003 is advised for 6–16-year-olds in high-transmission areas; vaccines supplement but do not replace vector control. Authorities will bolster surveillance and early intervention at hotspots.
