The session also stressed stronger prevention measures and early detection of suspected Ebola cases in schools, aiming to better protect students and school staff through improved school-based prevention practices in Ituri.

article.articleHeadline: India Unveils First Homegrown H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine To Protect ₹2.36-lakh-Crore Poultry Sector
article.articleSummary: India's first indigenous vaccine against highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) was unveiled by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal. The inactivated vaccine, tested in specific-pathogen-free layer and grower chickens, provides protection for up to six months and blocks transmission to contact birds. Trials met sterility, safety and efficacy standards, and the technology is ready for commercial production. Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan called it a historic achievement. The Rs 2.36 lakh crore poultry sector has endured about 500 outbreaks since 2006, causing losses of Rs 2,220–3,000 crore and triggering mass culling. India is the world’s second-largest egg producer and fourth-largest broiler producer, with over 60 lakh small/medium farmers and around 3 lakh rural backyard households. Timely vaccination is expected to reduce infection spread and limit human exposure.

article.articleHeadline: Butembo: évaluation de la perception communautaire de la riposte Ebola dans une zone sanitaire - ACP

article.articleSummary: Butembo, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, hosted a community-score bulletin to gauge public perception of the Ebola response in the Butembo health zone amid the 17th Ebola outbreak. Civil society, youth, and community relay volunteers participated to compare community views with the health zone’s own assessment. The community scored the zone at 49.2%, while the health zone self-assessed at 85%, revealing a notable perception gap regarding response effectiveness. The most poorly rated aspects were rumor management by the health zone and the overall level of communication, each at 39.7%. The exercise also aimed to create an exchange framework to improve transparency and information flow. A Saturday public-expression forum was planned to ask questions and make recommendations on risk communication and community engagement. BENENFANCE Congo organized all sessions.

article.articleHeadline: Brazil's Measles Recovery Offers U.S. Route Back to Elimination | EconoTimes
article.articleSummary: Measles: United States lost its elimination status after 12 months of endemic transmission (Jan 20, 2025–Jan 20, 2026); PAHO announced Nov 17 that the U.S., Mexico and Bolivia re-established endemic transmission. CDC reported 5,412 confirmed U.S. cases, 5,216 outbreaks (96%), and 43 outbreaks in 2026 as of Nov 12, 2026. Kindergarten vaccination fell to 92.4% in 2025-2026 from 95.2% in 2019-2020; about 280,000 kindergartners remain unprotected. Brazil regained measles-elimination status in 2024 after a 2019 outbreak (21,700 cases) and recorded 70 confirmed cases in 2026, all linked to imported infections. Brazil’s approach combines routine vaccination with active case finding, contact tracing, rapid investigations; over 16 million MMR doses distributed to states and 500,000 additional doses to Peru; Dia S and Dia D campaigns near the Brazil–Colombia–Peru border. WHO notes 95% two-dose coverage needed; Brazil’s second-dose coverage was about 76% in 2025. CDC lauds strengthened U.S. surveillance and targeted vaccination; totals are preliminary.

article.articleHeadline: I virus che attaccano i batteri resistenti: sei nuovi fagi contro l'Escherichia coli
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The viruses that attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria: six new phages against Escherichia coli.
article.articleSummary: Six bacteriophages active against multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli were identified from hospital wastewater in China and, in vitro, infected resistant strains and disrupted pre-formed biofilms. Published in Frontiers in Microbiology, the work highlights phage therapy as a path toward personalized treatment for hard-to-treat infections, though lab results do not guarantee clinical success. Phages differ in adsorption speed, replication, and tolerance to temperature and acidity; no known antibiotic-resistance or virulence genes were detected, but safety and efficacy require clinical trials. Bacterial resistance to phages is possible, prompting exploration of phage cocktails. Complementary 2026 studies show the urinary environment influences phage and antibiotic activity against E. coli, guiding combination strategies. A European randomized trial assesses personalized phage therapy with antibiotics to prevent recurrent UTIs in women. If validated, phage therapy could augment treatment for resistant or recurrent infections by tailoring phages to the pathogen.

article.articleHeadline: Review Highlights Wildlife and Livestock Reservoirs Challenging Global
article.articleSummary: Global tuberculosis eradication is undermined by animal reservoirs. The review documents extensive circulation of Mycobacterium bovis and related MTBC members in domestic livestock and captive wildlife. In 2024 TB caused about 1.23 million deaths and 10.7 million infections worldwide; about 10–15% of TB cases in low- and middle-income countries are due to M. bovis (roughly 140,000–149,000 zoonotic cases 2016–2020). More than 20 million animals carry TB, and M. bovis may account for up to one in ten incident TB cases globally (≈1.8 million people in 2023). Other MTBC species include orygis, caprae, pinnipedii, microti, mungi, suricattae; M. orygis drives zoonotic TB in South Asia, with India reporting ~21.8 million cows infected with M. orygis. Diagnostics and therapy are impeded by non-differentiation in Xpert assays, slower culture for M. bovis, pyruvate requirements, and pyrazinamide resistance due to pncA mutations, complicating regimens. Transmission dynamics involve bidirectional animal–human interactions.

article.articleHeadline: Casos graves de Covid-19 voltam a crescer no Paraná, aponta Fiocruz
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Severe COVID-19 cases are rising again in Paraná, Fiocruz says.
article.articleSummary: In Paraná, COVID-19 activity rebounded after months of decline, with 413 severe COVID-19 hospitalizations and 47 deaths recorded in 2026 so far. The Fiocruz InfoGripe bulletin notes increases in COVID-19–associated Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) in Paraná and six Centro-Sul states (Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Espírito Santo, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul) during Epidemiological Week 45 (Nov 8–14), though overall incidence remains low. Curitiba is monitored but not listed among four cities with long‑term SRAG growth. A PJ.2.1 lineage circulates; in Rio de Janeiro it accounts for 58% of genomes (96/167) from Oct 17–Nov 6 and has also been detected in Distrito Federal, São Paulo, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul, and Espírito Santo, with no confirmed vaccine‑escape signal yet. Vaccination remains key; boosters every six months for elderly/immunocompromised, annual for others. Paraná will receive ~50,000 additional doses. Nationally, COVID-19 represented 15.5% of recent SRAG positives; rhinovirus led at 47.4%.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India Develops First Indigenous H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine, One Dose to Protect Chickens for Six Months | Chickens Will No Longer Have to Be Killed! India's Victory Over Bird Flu, One Dose of This Indigenous Vaccine Will Pay Off
article.articleSummary: India has developed the first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry, targeting the 2.3.2.1a H5N1 strain. The vaccine, produced by scientists at the ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal and dedicated to the nation by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, is designed to protect chickens for about six months from a single dose, especially laying and breeder stock. The eight-member team led by Dr. S. Nagarajan began work in September 2025. H5N1 is highly dangerous, with mortality in infected flocks potentially reaching 100%, leading to culling and severe economic losses. The indigenous vaccine is expected to reduce dependence on foreign vaccines, lowering outbreak risk and associated poultry-sector disruption, and it may also reduce the spillover risk of the virus to humans by preventing poultry infections.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in Congo has claimed 5,500 lives as scientists reveal its mysterious characteristics.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has reached about 11,000 confirmed infections and 5,500 deaths after more than six months, with no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. The outbreak is spreading roughly twice as fast as West Africa's 2014-2016 epidemic. WHO and the Africa CDC warn the danger lies in deceptive symptoms: only 5–10% of confirmed cases exhibit internal or external bleeding, leading to misdiagnosis and delays in care, with an estimated 70% of victims dying in local communities before reaching health facilities. Children under five are disproportionately affected: 1,207 confirmed infections and 844 deaths, a case fatality rate near 70%, versus about 50% in adults. Genetic sequencing shows no rapid mutation, but humanitarian and security challenges in eastern DRC hinder data collection and early detection, according to Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF).

article.articleSummary: In eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola continues to affect schools. Six months into the outbreak, the virus is spreading geographically, especially in conflict-affected areas, with WHO reporting roughly 400–500 new cases weekly. The ECDC tallies over 11,500 confirmed cases and 5,600 deaths since May. Health authorities say insecurity hampers containment, while WHO has declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. As of 20 November 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国東部で約100校がエボラの影響を受ける
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言した大規模エボラ流行であり、学校感染拡大・高致死率・紛争地域での封じ込め困難などIHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: WHOが既にPHEICを宣言済みの進行中アウトブレイクであり、累計11,500例・死亡5,600例と深刻。学校を含む地域コミュニティへの感染拡大が継続している。

article.articleHeadline: Morte de detento por Covid-19 leva à interdição de ala em presídio de BH
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death of an inmate from COVID-19 leads to the closure of a wing at a Belo Horizonte prison.
article.articleSummary: A 23-year-old inmate died in Belo Horizonte after being diagnosed with COVID-19 while being treated for pneumonia; the death led to the preventive closure of the wing at Ceresp Gameleira, with inmates in the affected gallery to be tested for respiratory symptoms. The Minas Gerais Penitentiary Department transferred entry duties for male prisoners in Belo Horizonte to Complexo Penitenciário Nelson Hungria in Contagem, so new detainees are temporarily received in Contagem. The measure follows a regional surge in respiratory illnesses: Contagem saw a 21.3% rise in the average daily emergency visits in November versus October. In Minas Gerais, confirmed COVID-19 cases rose to 1,903 in November from 910 in October (about 109% increase) per preliminary Health Ministry data. Health authorities also urged mask use in health facilities.

triage.headline_ja: 受刑者のCOVID-19死亡によりベロオリゾンテの刑務所の一画が閉鎖
triage.triage_reason: 刑務所内での単発死亡事例だが、ミナスジェライス州全体で呼吸器疾患・COVID-19症例が増加傾向にあり、閉鎖環境での感染拡大リスクがあるため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 刑務所という閉鎖的・密集環境での感染は拡大しやすいが、現時点では単一死亡例であり地域当局により管理されている。州全体でのCOVID-19症例の109%増加は注視すべき動向。

article.articleHeadline: Acceden a la parte más letal del mecanismo del virus del ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: They access the most lethal part of the Ebola virus's mechanism.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease has about 50% fatality in humans. The current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,000 confirmed cases and around 5,400 deaths. Researchers from the La Jolla Institute for Immunology (LJI), in collaboration with Princeton University and UC San Diego, pinpoint why humans are more vulnerable. Using spatial transcriptomics, they show that Ebola builds membraneless condensates inside host cells that trap host mRNA, including many that encode type I interferon (IFN) response genes. When these transcripts are sequestered, the inflammatory response spirals out of control, triggering cytokine overproduction, organ failure, and death. In bats, mRNA folding differs, so transcripts are not trapped, allowing infection to be controlled and the animals to remain asymptomatic. The virus also harbors its own viral mRNA within these compartments. Findings published in Cell.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスメカニズムの最も致命的な部分へのアクセス
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外な病理メカニズムの発見、国際的拡大リスク）。コンゴでの継続的なアウトブレイク（11,000確認症例、5,400死亡）と、ウイルスの致命的メカニズムに関する重要な科学的発見が合致し、シグナル価値が高い。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴでの現在のエボラアウトブレイク（11,000確認症例、5,400死亡）と、La Jolla Institute for Immunologyによる病理メカニズムの重要な発見を報告している。La Jollaはカリフォルニアにあるため米国内の研究機関であり、アウトブレイクの発生地はDRCのみ。ウイルスの致命的メカニズムに関する新知見は感染症危機管理に重要な意味を持つ。

article.articleHeadline: Ouro Preto confirma 95 casos de Covid em três dias e cria comitê de crise
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ouro Preto confirms 95 COVID-19 cases in three days and forms a crisis committee.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Ouro Preto, Brazil: 95 cases confirmed between Monday, Nov 16 and Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026, per the first municipal epidemiological bulletin released Nov 19 via the city's social media. No deaths and no cases of severe acute respiratory syndrome (SRAG) associated with coronavirus in this period. The municipality notes a rising trend in cases locally and nationwide. A crisis committee was formed on Nov 18 to monitor progression and coordinate response. The Municipal Health Secretariat will publish weekly case counts going forward. Bulletin data come from the city’s Epidemiological Surveillance unit; earlier weekly figures were not disclosed, so the magnitude of the increase cannot be quantified from this report.

triage.headline_ja: オウロ・プレト市、3日間でCOVID-19症例95件を確認し危機対策委員会を設置
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の局地的な増加が報告されているが、死亡や重症例はなく、既知の病原体による国内の季節的な変動である可能性が高いため、フルRRAには至らないが続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 既知の病原体（COVID-19）による地方都市レベルの症例増加。死亡・重症例なし。危機対策委員会設置は地方自治体レベルの対応であり、国際的な懸念事項には該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Solan: नालागढ़ के इस गांव में अचानक बीमार पड़ रहे थे लोग, लैब से आई रिपोर्ट में 3 ग्रामीण निकले डेंगू पॉजिटिव
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Solan: In this village in Nalagarh, people were suddenly falling ill; three villagers tested positive for dengue in the lab report.
article.articleSummary: Three residents from Lakhiredo Vas village, Baruna Gram Panchayat in Nalagarh's industrial area, Solan district, Himachal Pradesh, have dengue-positive lab reports after an outbreak. Earlier, 23 villagers underwent rapid dengue screening; 9 tested positive. The nine samples were sent to a Parwanoo laboratory for confirmation, which confirmed 3 dengue-positive cases. Health authorities plan a Saturday field visit to monitor and test the infected individuals’ platelet counts; the patients are in private hospitals, with government hospital care arranged if needed. No deaths were reported. This marks a localized dengue outbreak in Baruna/Lakhiredo Vas, with laboratory confirmation from Parwanoo and ongoing health surveillance. Public health measures are ongoing, including vector control and public awareness efforts.

triage.headline_ja: ソラン：ナーラーガルのこの村で人々が突然病気になり、検査報告で3人の村人がデング熱陽性と判明
triage.triage_reason: インドの一地方村落における小規模なデング熱発生（陽性3名、死亡なし）であり、季節性かつ局所的な事象で、IHR基準・社会的関心基準ともに該当しない。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドにおいて地方病的に発生しており、本件は村単位の小規模クラスター。死亡例なく、地元保健当局が対応中（媒介蚊対策・住民啓発）。続報の必要性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Casos de covid crescem no Brasil mesmo com vacina sobrando
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 cases are rising in Brazil, even with vaccines in abundance.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 cases are rising in Brazil across 19 states for six consecutive weeks, though overall risk remains low. Between Jan 1 and Nov 15, 2026, 135,740 influenza-like illnesses due to COVID-19 were reported; actual numbers are likely undercounted. Fiocruz's InfoGripe bulletin notes increased severe cases in Mato Grosso, Distrito Federal, Santa Catarina, Bahia, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. By Nov 9, 2026, 3,641 severe cases and 445 deaths were recorded nationally. The predominant virus variant is XFG, a descendant of Omicron, responsible for about 90% of cases. Vaccination uptake is low: 21.9 million doses distributed in 2025; only 8 million administered, far short of the 15 million target. Vaccines remain effective at preventing severe disease, despite waning immunity and emerging variants; boosters advised for older adults and immunocompromised groups. Contributing factors include reduced risk perception and misinformation.

triage.headline_ja: ワクチンが余っているにもかかわらず、ブラジルでCOVID-19症例が増加
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル国内でCOVID-19（オミクロン系統XFG）の症例が6週連続で増加しているが、記事自体が「全体リスクは低い」と明記しており、新規性・異常性は乏しい。ただしワクチン接種率の低さや重症化例の増加があり、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 既知の季節的COVID-19流行（オミクロン系統XFGが主流）であり、記事内でも全体リスクは低いと評価されている。ワクチン接種率の低迷と重症化・死亡例の増加が継続的な懸念材料。新規性・国際的拡大の兆候は確認されない。

article.articleHeadline: Actualité | Sud-Kivu : la campagne de vaccination contre la poliomyélite reportée au 26 novembre | mediacongo.net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: News | South Kivu: Polio vaccination campaign postponed to November 26 | mediacongo.net
article.articleSummary: Polio vaccination campaign in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, postponed from November 19–21, 2026 to November 26–29, 2026, covering 34 health zones around Bukavu. More than two million children aged 0–5 are targeted. The delay follows logistical constraints in delivering vaccines across health zones, prompted by a poliovirus notification in Kitutu health zone, Mwenga territory, highlighting the need for rapid preventive action. Vaccination teams will conduct door-to-door visits, administering the vaccine to all children in the target age group, regardless of prior vaccination status. The operation is organized by the provincial health division and is free of charge. Dr. Michel Maneno urged parents and guardians to ensure vaccination for all eligible children. Poliomyelitis is a highly contagious viral disease that can cause irreversible paralysis, underscoring the campaign’s public health importance.

triage.headline_ja: ニュース | 南キブ州：ポリオワクチン接種キャンペーンが11月26日に延期 | mediacongo.net
triage.triage_reason: DRC南キブ州のキトゥト保健地区でポリオウイルスの新規検出が報告され、大規模ワクチン接種キャンペーンの延期という公衆衛生対応が生じており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はワクチン接種キャンペーンの延期を主題としているが、その背景にキトゥト保健地区（ムウェンガ準州）でのポリオウイルス検出がある。ポリオはIHR(2005)上、国際的懸念対象の疾患であり、DRCは継続的なcVDPV流行国でもあるため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: சிவகங்கையில் 1.2 லட்சம் குழந்தைகளுக்கு போலியோ சொட்டு மருந்து முகாம்: பெற்றோர்களே, உங்கள் கடமை!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Polio drops vaccination camp for 1.2 lakh children in Sivagangai: Parents, your duty!
article.articleSummary: Polio vaccination drive underway in Sivaganga district, Tamil Nadu, targeting all children under five. On 22 November 2026 (Sunday), 1,270 vaccination sites across the district—1,197 permanent centers (government hospitals, primary health centers, urban health centers, Anganwadi centers, and schools), 54 mobile centers, and 19 intermediate locations at bus stands, railway stations, and customs checkpoints—will administer oral polio drops to about 101,513 children. If any child is missed, door-to-door campaigns will operate on 23–24 November 2026. Preparations include maintaining cold-chain and transport of vaccines, ensuring space and sanitation at centers, and dedicated department vehicles. A total of 5,404 staff from health, social welfare, integrated child development services, rural and urban development, education and other departments will support; over 150 medical officers and supervisors will monitor the campaign. District Collector P. Akash urged that even if children have already received drops, they should be vaccinated again to help eradicate polio.

triage.headline_ja: シヴァガンガイで12万人の子供にポリオワクチン接種キャンプ：保護者の皆様、義務を果たしてください！
triage.triage_reason: 通常のポリオ予防接種キャンペーンの実施告知であり、症例発生や異常事態の報告ではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事は通常の予防接種活動（ポリオ経口ワクチン投与キャンペーン）の告知であり、ポリオ症例の発生や発生の報告は含まれていない。地域行政による定例的な公衆衛生活動のため対象国リストに該当する発生事例として扱わない。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox pode ser transmitida por objetos e atinge pessoas com baixa imunidade, alerta médico
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mpox can be transmitted through objects and affects immunocompromised individuals, doctors warn.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) in Brazil: As of 16 November 2026, Brazil reported 1,055 confirmed mpox cases and one death, per the Ministério da Saúde. In an interview on Agora (TV Meio Norte), infectious-disease specialist Luciano Mourão explained that mpox spreads through close contact and contaminated objects, not solely via sexual activity among men who have sex with men. Transmission can occur during sexual contact without protection and also via fomites such as bedding, utensils, and other shared items. The disease can be more severe in immunocompromised individuals, including older adults, infants, and people living with HIV with weakened immunity. Early symptoms appear 3–5 days to up to two weeks after exposure and include flu-like signs (fever, headache, malaise) followed by skin lesions that become vesicles and eventually crusts. Unlike varicella, all lesions are identical.

triage.headline_ja: Mpoxは物を介して感染する可能性があり、免疫力の低い人に影響を与える、と医師が警告
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルで継続中のMpox流行に関する一般啓発記事であり、新規性・異常性は低いが、死亡例を含む症例数の報告があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル国内の既存Mpox流行（累計1,055例、死亡1例）に関する医師への啓発インタビューであり、新規アウトブレイクや異常事象の報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Hepatitis B Virus ER Stress Suppresses Secretion of Antiviral Protein
article.articleSummary: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress from hepatitis B virus infection promotes intracellular retention of viral components and impairs their secretion, delaying clearance and increasing hepatocellular injury. A translational study evaluated how ER stress affects C-type lectin 18 (CLEC18), an innate antiviral secretory protein that resides in the ER, Golgi, and endosomes and acts as a Toll-like receptor 3 coreceptor to boost interferon responses. In a retrospective clinical evaluation at China Medical University Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan, 121 treatment-naive adults with chronic HBV and 17 healthy controls were analyzed across clinical phases: immune tolerance, immune clearance, and treated or spontaneous seroconversion. HBV DNA peaked during immune clearance (9.3 log10 IU/mL) and became undetectable after seroconversion; ALT reached 458 U/L in immune clearance and 361 U/L during e-antigen seroconversion on therapy. Baseline CLEC18 was lowest in inactive phases (≈215 pg/mL), higher during immune clearance (≈871 pg/mL) and seroconversion (treated ≈799 pg/mL; spontaneous resolvers ≈1538 pg/mL), with healthy controls exceeding immune-tolerance levels. Findings link ER-stress–driven secretion defects to dynamic CLEC18 kinetics and antiviral defense across HBV infection phases.

triage.headline_ja: B型肺炎ウイルス感染による小胞体ストレスが抗ウイルスタンパク質CLEC18の分泌を抑制する
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は基礎研究・臨床観察研究であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性やアウトブレイクに関する情報はなく、トリアージ対象のシグナルには該当しない。
triage.notes: 台湾の病院で行われた慢性B型肝炎患者を対象とした分子生物学・臨床研究であり、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の脅威を示す内容ではない。台湾は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: Rims gets Rs 2.3cr modern lab to boost TB diagnosis & treatment
article.articleSummary: Rs 2.30 crore BSL-III microbiology laboratory inaugurated at Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Ranchi, Jharkhand, under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme. Facility will conduct mycobacterial culture and drug susceptibility testing to identify drugs TB is sensitive or resistant to, strengthening diagnosis and treatment of multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) and drug-resistant TB, and reducing patients’ need to travel outside Jharkhand. Advanced biosafety features include negative air pressure, unidirectional airflow and HEPA filtration to protect staff and prevent spread of infectious agents. RIMS is positioned to integrate modern diagnostics, digital health infrastructure and AI, with aims to become a leading medical institution. Minister Irfan Ansari also laid the foundation for renovation/expansion of the OPD/IPD building, targeted for completion within two years to ease patient load.

triage.headline_ja: RIMSに結核診断・治療強化のための最新鋭ラボ、2.3千万ルピーで設置
triage.triage_reason: 新規検査施設の開設に関する行政・インフラ整備のニュースであり、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はジャールカンド州ランチーにおける結核診断ラボの開設という医療インフラ整備のニュースであり、感染症アウトブレイクのシグナルではない。

article.articleHeadline: India develops first indigenous H5N1 vaccine for chickens
article.articleSummary: India's ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal developed the country's first indigenous inactivated H5N1 vaccine for chickens, targeting clade 2.3.2.1a and tailored to strains circulating in India. The Ministry of Agriculture announced on 18 November that Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan would dedicate the vaccine on 20 November, with technology transfer the same day. The vaccine addresses a variant with no current commercial vaccine. Since 2006, India has reported more than 500 outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 in poultry, with the 2006 outbreak causing direct and indirect losses estimated at Rs 2,200–3,000 crore. HPAI can trigger culling, movement restrictions and disruption of production and markets; infections have occurred in other animals and in three humans. No details were given on manufacturers, capacity, price, supply timelines or national rollout; vaccination would need to accompany surveillance, biosecurity and prompt reporting.

triage.headline_ja: インドが鶏用の国産初H5N1ワクチンを開発
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は新規アウトブレイクの発生報告ではなく、インドが鶏用H5N1ワクチンを開発したという技術開発・政策ニュースであり、現在進行中の公衆衛生上の脅威を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は2006年以降のインドにおける500件超のH5N1/H5N8家禽アウトブレイク歴と、過去に3人のヒト感染があったことに言及しているが、これは背景情報であり、現在進行中の新規発生ではない。主題はワクチン開発・技術移転のポジティブな政策ニュースである。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : deux zones de santé confrontées à une couverture insuffisante contre Ebola - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: two health zones facing insufficient coverage against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Two health zones in Ituri, Mangala and Mandima, in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, still lack full coverage of Ebola virus disease response interventions across the pillars, according to a strategic coordination meeting report. The document notes concerns over incomplete coverage by the Ebola response pillars and calls for stronger coordination and greater mobilization of human, material, and financial resources in these zones. Participants urged technical and financial partners to extend support to underserved areas in Mambasa territory to ensure a more equitable distribution of interventions and improve the population's response to needs. The report, signed by Father Justin Njango, provincial supervisor of National Education and Citizenship Ituri 1, underscores the ongoing imperative to bolster the response. Published: 20 November 2026.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ州：2つの保健地域でエボラ対策のカバレッジ不足に直面
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州における進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク対応において、2つの保健地域で介入のカバレッジ不足が指摘されており、IHR基準（重大な公衆衛生影響、異常事態）に複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCイトゥリ州マンバサ地域（マンガラ・マンディマ保健地域）におけるエボラ対応の調整会議報告に基づく。南オーストラリア州・オーストラリアはBluedotの発生地域に含まれるが、記事内容とは無関係のため除外した。

triage.headline_ja: なぜエボラウイルスはヒトに致死的で、コウモリは無症状のままなのか？
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は主にエボラウイルスの病原性メカニズムに関する基礎研究（コウモリとヒトの免疫応答の違い）を扱う科学解説記事であり、新規の流行イベントの報告ではない。ただし文中でコンゴ民主共和国における進行中のエボラ流行（確定症例10,500人超、死者5,130人超）が言及されており、規模が非常に大きいため継続的な注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : le déploiement des pédiatres dans les écoles sollicité afin de prévenir Ebola - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: Deployment of pediatricians in schools requested to prevent Ebola - ACP
article.articleSummary: In Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo (Bunia), Ebola prevention in schools is being prioritized, with a pilot deployment of pediatricians. Lipeco-RDC president Etienne Amani advocates technical validation, school access, and partner funding to implement a three-month pilot in ten Bunia schools, deploying about twenty pediatricians to bolster student health surveillance and Ebola prevention. The approach extends beyond temperature checks to assess children’s health, recognize alert signs, and arrange rapid referrals to health facilities, while keeping schools from diagnosing or taking samples. A coordinated effort between the Ministries of Health and Education is sought to strengthen school health services and implement the initiative. Teachers report concerns; pediatricians provide health orientation; parents and rapid-response teams cooperate under official protocols. If Ebola is suspected, the child is protected and discreetly referred to appropriate health services to avoid stigma.

article.articleHeadline: Casos de escabiose atingem ao menos 40 municípios em MG
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases of scabies reach at least 40 municipalities in Minas Gerais
article.articleSummary: By 19 November 2026, Minas Gerais state in Brazil reported at least 40 municipalities with human scabies cases, up from 11 a month earlier. Most cases are unresolved, with official counts pending review by Primary Health Care; diagnosis is largely clinical. Outbreaks were linked to Sete Lagoas and Andradas, prompting temporary school closures in late Sept/early Oct; cases now span the central, central-west, and southern regions, including Belo Horizonte and its metropolitan area, Ouro Preto, Poços de Caldas, and Varginha. Scabies is caused by Sarcoptes scabiei and spreads through close skin contact and contact with contaminated textiles. People should seek care at a Basic Health Unit; treatment is available orally and topically. Prevention: wash daily clothes, bed linens, and towels in water at least 55°C; seal items that cannot be washed in plastic bags for at least one week; close contacts may require treatment; itching may persist weeks after treatment.

article.articleHeadline: Plus de 1 730 enfants décédés d'Ebola en RDC (Unicef) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 1,730 children have died of Ebola in the DRC (UNICEF) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: More than 1,730 children have died from Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo six months after the outbreak was declared, according to UNICEF. The current outbreak—derived from Bundibugyo lineage—is the largest and deadliest in the DRC, spanning eight provinces: North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Uélé (Upper Uele), Bas-Uele (Lower Uele), Tshopo, Sud Ubangi, and Nord-Ubangi. Since the declaration, the country has reported 11,613 laboratory-confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths. The surge has left many children orphaned or separated from caregivers and disrupted protection, health, nutrition, vaccination, education, water and sanitation, and child-protection services, amid ongoing conflict and displacement. UNICEF and partners are intensifying response, strengthening surveillance, early detection, prevention and infection control, and ensuring continuity of essential services for children and communities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラにより1,730人以上の子どもが死亡（ユニセフ）- ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大・最悪規模とされるエボラ流行が継続中で、死者数・感染者数が甚大かつ複数州に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 本流行はBundibugyo株由来でDRC史上最大規模とされ、紛争・住民避難と重なり対応が困難化。ユニセフは子どもの保護・保健・栄養・ワクチン接種等のサービス継続支援を強化している。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Beni : le respect strict des mesures barrières exigé aux clients d'un restaurant - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Beni: strict adherence to barrier measures required of restaurant customers.
article.articleSummary: Ebola prevention measures are being strictly enforced for customers at a Restau Bar Palma in Boikene, Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Owner Mario Clavdianos reports entry includes hand sanitizer and optional handwashing, with rigorous cleanliness in toilets and all areas; customers must disinfect hands after handling money or objects, and vegetables bought at the market should be washed to prevent transmission. The establishment uses posters and direct conversations to raise awareness, with servers ensuring hand disinfection before access to facilities. Clavdianos urges other bar owners to reduce crowding and maintain adequate distancing, even for groups. He emphasizes that Ebola requires individual and collective responsibility and that prevention hinges on hygiene and adherence to health-service guidelines. The article underscores the seriousness of Ebola and ongoing community preventive efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Sorocaba adere à Semana Nacional de Combate ao Aedes Aegypti - Agência de Notícias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sorocaba joins National Week to Combat Aedes aegypti - News Agency.
article.articleSummary: Sorocaba's Health Secretariat joins the National Week to Combat Aedes aegypti to boost prevention and control of arboviruses from Monday, November 23 to Friday, November 27, 2026, with Saturday activities on November 28. Zoonoses teams will intensify inspections at recyclable and scrap-collection sites, perform nebulization where there is a positive or suspected arbovirus case, and conduct home visits to guide residents and remove potential breeding sites, aided by three trucks for removing water-collecting materials. On Tuesday, November 24, at 13:00, epidemiological surveillance will train health professionals at UFSCar Santa Rosália. Saturday’s Day D runs 9:00–13:00 with educational displays at Parque da Água Vermelha (João Câncio Pereira) and CEI-17 Issa Latuf (Jardim Sandra); another Zoonoses team will inspect properties 8:00–14:00. Breeding-site reports can be filed via 156, the city site, Casas do Cidadão, or WhatsApp (15) 99691-2783. Rabies control blocks are listed for Jardim Faculdade and Casa Branca.

article.articleHeadline: Ouro Preto registra 95 casos de Covid-19 em três dias e cria comitê de crise para acompanhar doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ouro Preto records 95 COVID-19 cases in three days and creates a crisis committee to monitor the disease.
article.articleSummary: Ouro Preto, Brazil, reports 95 confirmed COVID-19 cases between 16 and 18 November 2026, with no deaths or SRAG cases. The municipal health department released its first epidemiological bulletin on 20 November and on 18 November formed a crisis committee to monitor the trend. To keep residents informed, weekly epidemiological bulletins will be published. The Health Secretariat emphasizes vaccination for priority groups: people aged 60+, children 6 months to 5 years, individuals with comorbidities or immunocompromised states, pregnant and puerperal women, and health workers. Booster doses are available at reference health units; residents should bring the vaccination card to verify pending doses. The Vacimóvel mobile vaccination unit is parked at UPA Dom Orione, operating Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. Preventive guidance includes avoiding crowds, frequent hand hygiene, and masking in indoor or high-traffic areas.

article.articleHeadline: CASOS DE MPOX CRESCEM NO BRASIL
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mpox cases rise in Brazil.
article.articleSummary: As of 16 November 2026, Brazil reports 1,055 confirmed mpox cases, with São Paulo leading (398), Rio de Janeiro (391), and Minas Gerais (41), and one death in Rio de Janeiro. Mpox (monkeypox) is caused by the monkeypox virus and presents with fever, headache, muscle pain, fatigue, lymphadenopathy, and skin or mucosal lesions. Transmission is mainly via direct contact with infected lesions, secretions, and bodily fluids, and via contaminated objects such as towels, clothing, and bed linens. The Ministry of Health maintains surveillance, reinforces vaccination for priority groups, and promotes prevention and early diagnosis. People with symptoms or close contact with suspected cases are advised to seek health care. Numbers this year remain below the 2022 peak of 10,591 cases and 14 deaths in Brazil.

article.articleHeadline: 中國疫情肆虐 青壯年心肺受損喪失勞動力 | 新冠病毒 | 反覆感染 | 心力衰竭
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's outbreak ravages prime-age adults: cardiopulmonary damage and loss of work capacity | COVID-19 | recurrent infections | heart failure
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 recurrences are driving severe cardiopulmonary damage among working-age adults across China, with repeated infections worsening heart and lung function. In Shaanxi, a 36-year-old man with heart failure reports multiple infections and symptoms—cough, phlegm, chest tightness, then asthma-like deterioration—despite treatment. In Henan, a woman just over 40 developed progressive heart failure during lockdown and underwent a heart transplant this year after collapsing fatigue and immobility. In Hebei, a physician in his early 30s contracted the virus repeatedly; after interstitial pneumonia, he requires 24-hour oxygen and faces possible lung transplantation due to substantial lung injury. In Heilongjiang, a 50-year-old man with COPD and coronary disease has recurrent pneumonia this year, living largely on oxygen with cognitive and mobility decline. The report emphasizes the lack of a definitive cure and highlights alarming long-term sequelae from recurrent infections. Location mentions include Shaanxi, Henan, Hebei, and Heilongjiang."} }{}{

article.articleHeadline: 6 மாவட்டங்களில் நாளை போலியோ சிறப்பு முகாம்
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Special Polio Camp in Six Districts Tomorrow.
article.articleSummary: Oral polio vaccine (OPV) drops will be distributed in Tamil Nadu on Sunday, November 22, from 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, targeting 9.16 lakh children under five across six districts: Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai, Thanjavur, Sivaganga, Tirunelveli, and Virudhunagar. The nationwide plan, endorsed by India’s Polio Expert Advisory Group, aims to conduct special polio camps in 272 districts to sustain eradication, even as neighboring countries report cases. Vaccinations will be offered at health facilities, public venues, schools and colleges, private hospitals, and via mobile camps. Children who were vaccinated earlier should also receive the drops at these camps. To verify eligibility, each child’s left-hand index finger will be marked with ink. Over 27,000 personnel are involved in the operation.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Avian influenza: First domestically produced vaccine for chickens introduced.
article.articleSummary: On Friday, 20 November 2026, Madhya Pradesh, Bhopal, saw the introduction of the first domestically produced vaccine for chickens against avian influenza. The H5N1 vaccine, developed by the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) in Bhopal, targets the clade 2.3.2.1a of H5N1. Madhya Pradesh Sports Minister Vishvas Sarang and BJP MP Alok Sharma were among those present. Officials said this marks a major milestone in poultry health and farmer livelihoods, as avian influenza (HPAI) has nearly 100% mortality in affected birds and causes substantial economic losses. Since 2006, more than 500 outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 have been reported domestically. The domestically produced vaccine is expected to bolster the country’s disease-control efforts and protect poultry stocks.

article.articleHeadline: Água da Sabesp tem bactéria fecal em 68 municípios de São Paulo após privatização
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sabesp's water contains fecal bacteria in 68 municipalities in the state of São Paulo after privatization.
article.articleSummary: Escherichia coli contamination was detected in Sabesp’s treated water across 68 municipalities in São Paulo state from January to September 2026, after privatization. E. coli appeared in 137 samples; São Paulo city had 21 positives, and São José dos Campos nine (all in the first half), with subsequent retests showing negative results. Arsesp and Sabesp said most samples met potability standards; in São José dos Campos, 5,737 analyses yielded 99.84% conformity. The Health Ministry standard requires zero E. coli per 100 mL and uses positive results to trigger investigations. In Itapeva, Cryptosporidium was identified in water from four regions, contributing to more than 4,300 gastroenteritis-related visits since September and a state of calamity declared on November 6. Sabesp has pledged about R$50 million to install ultrafiltration; Itapeva has distributed potable water by trucks. Some cases’ link to water remains unproven.

triage.notes: 水道水の民営化後の品質問題と、Itapevaでの胃腸炎集団発生・州の非常事態宣言が中心的話題。国際的拡大の可能性は低いが、公衆衛生上の影響と行政対応の規模から注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya Discharges Final Ebola Patient
article.articleSummary: Kenya discharged its final Ebola patient, moving toward declaring the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak over. Nine confirmed cases: seven recovered, two died. The last patient was discharged November 11, 2026, starting a 42-day countdown that began November 12 toward a December 23 declaration if no new cases emerge. The outbreak began with an imported Kenyan national who traveled from the DRC through Uganda, linked to four family members and four healthcare workers. All 135 contacts were traced and monitored; eight subsequent infections occurred while their bearers were already in quarantine. The final confirmed case was October 19, and the remaining 11 contacts were released after completing 21 days. Kenya will maintain heightened surveillance, entry-point screening, rapid response teams, survivor support, and public awareness; no domestic restrictions were announced. The broader regional outbreak remains a concern with ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease in the DRC.

article.articleHeadline: Sarna humana é registrada em ao menos 12 cidades de MS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Human scabies has been recorded in at least 12 cities in Mato Grosso do Sul.
article.articleSummary: Human scabies has been recorded in at least 12 cities in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. Nine municipalities—Dourados, Itaporã, Douradina, Batayporã, Campo Grande, Jardim, Aparecida do Taboado, Paranaíba and Angélica—have officially informed the Secretaria Estadual de Saúde of increased cases; Amambai, Nova Andradina and Rio Brilhante reported locally but not yet to the SES. The Ministry of Health is providing support. The epidemiological alert notes rising cases in schools and childcare centers; an outbreak is defined as three or more linked cases in a single environment, with 24-hour reporting for suspected outbreaks. Transmission is via prolonged skin-to-skin contact and sharing recently used clothing, linens, or towels. Symptoms include intense nocturnal itching and red lesions; adults often between fingers and wrists, infants may involve scalp and face. Diagnosis is clinical; treatment should start for patient and contacts simultaneously, with washing of clothes and bedding from the prior three days. School return usually the day after treatment, and surveillance lasts six weeks after last exposure.

article.articleHeadline: Small Molecules Target Nucleocapsid Protein to Block Crimean-Congo
article.articleSummary: Small-molecule inhibitors target the Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) nucleocapsid (N) protein, disrupting RNA encapsidation and N-mediated viral mRNA translation in cell culture. A high-throughput screen of 108,947 compounds yielded 122 inhibitors, 86 dose-responsive, and 37 confirmed hits; three were prioritized (11, 14, 33). In vitro, they noncompetitively inhibit N binding to the 5' UTR hairpin with IC50 11–41 μM and show CC50 >1–2 mM. In the Hazara virus surrogate (BSL-2), EC50s are 23–51 μM with selectivity indices 34–86. Plaque assays revealed >100-fold reductions for 11 and 14; 33 nearly abolishes detectable virus. Mechanistic assays indicate activity in post-entry replication by blocking N-mediated translation enhancement without disrupting host translation. Modeling points to compound 11 binding the N stalk–head interface (Gln300, Glu240, Lys473). These compounds offer leads for optimization; there are no approved antivirals or vaccines for CCHFV.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola dans la Tshopo: un agent de riposte agressé à Kisangani - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Tshopo Province: a member of the Ebola response team assaulted in Kisangani - ACP.
article.articleSummary: On 20 November 2026, in Kisangani, the provincial capital of Tshopo Province in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, an Ebola response team member from the risk communication pillar (CREC) was assaulted on the 2nd Avenue in a Kisangani commune. The attack followed delays in ambulance arrival to the scene while a person suspected of Ebola was to be transferred to an Ebola Treatment Center (CTE); the CREC agent sustained upper-body injuries and was reported bloodied. The family of the Ebola-suspected individual had agreed to transfer a relative to the CTE for care. The incident reflects a pattern of assaults on Ebola responders, attributed to community distrust, rumors, cultural constraints, and armed insecurity. The report also notes a call to decentralize ambulance management by affected zones to reduce delays and tensions during the outbreak response.

article.articleHeadline: Instituto Butantan cria Centro de Tecnologia em Arbovírus para estudar e combater sequelas crônicas de chikungunya, dengue e zika - Catanduva Na Net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Butantan Institute creates Center for Arbovirus Technology to study and combat chronic sequelae of chikungunya, dengue, and Zika.
article.articleSummary: São Paulo's Butantan Institute established the Center for Arbovirus Technology (CeTA) to study and combat chronic sequelae of chikungunya (CHIKV), dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), and yellow fever (YFV). The project targets molecular factors underlying inflammatory, neurological, and joint manifestations, with chikungunya capable of causing disabling arthritis—a major public health issue. Funded for five years by FAPESP and the institute, CeTA unites virologists, molecular biologists, and bioinformaticians with NB3 containment labs and Biobank, and collaborates with the Ragon Institute (MIT/MGH/Harvard) and CNPEM/LNBio (Sirius, Campinas). It relies on cellular/molecular biology, genetics, and AI/ML to map targets, develop predictive models, and perform 3D structural analyses of viral-human receptor interactions. Goals include validating at least three targets and advancing two biotherapeutics or vaccine candidates to late preclinical stage, using 3D human models, to strengthen Brazil's SUS and health sovereignty. Worldwide, about four billion people are at risk for dengue and arboviruses.

article.articleHeadline: Parque da Cidade recebe ação de prevenção e vacinação contra dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Parque da Cidade hosts dengue prevention and vaccination campaign.
article.articleSummary: Free dengue prevention and vaccination activities at Parque da Cidade Sarah Kubitschek in Brasília, Distrito Federal, Brazil, on Friday 20 and Saturday 21 November 2026. The Takeda-sponsored Vila da Prevenção provides a family-oriented circuit (15–30 minutes per activity) with games and discussions about dengue transmission, Aedes aegypti control, and prevention, guided by monitors. The Brasília edition coincides with the National Dengue Fight Day on 21 November, highlighting public and government action ahead of summer when transmission rises. On Saturday, 21 November, free dengue vaccination for youths aged 10–14 will be offered by the Governo do Distrito Federal from 09:00 to 16:00 at the same park. No pre-registration is required for the Vila da Prevenção. Location: Parque da Cidade Sarah Kubitschek, Setor de Recreação Pública Sul (SRPS), Asa Sul, Brasília.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola au Nord-Kivu: mise en service d'un nouveau centre de traitement à Bulongo - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in North Kivu: Commissioning of a New Treatment Center in Bulongo - ACP
article.articleSummary: An Ebola Treatment Center (ETC) with about 48 beds was inaugurated in Bulongo, a rural commune in Beni territory, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, on 20 November 2026. The facility, built by Ugandan engineers and technicians, will admit patients from the Mutwanga health zone and border communities along the Congo-Uganda frontier on the Beni–Mutwanga–Kasindi axis. The commissioning was led by a senior provincial health official representing the North Kivu military governor. Bulongo’s mayor highlighted Ugandan cooperation and described the center as the second ETC in DRC after the one at Butembo (ITAV site). The ETC aims to stop the spread of Ebola in Mutwanga and across the border, with authorities urging residents to protect themselves and noting ongoing cross-border collaboration with Uganda.

article.articleHeadline: Study Identifies Ten Percent Bacterial STI Rate Among Eastern China Clinic
article.articleSummary: Jiangsu Province, eastern China, a multi-center cross-sectional study of 2,661 male STI-clinic attendees (April–June 2023) found 10.30% with at least one bacterial STI (syphilis, Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae). Among tests, total syphilis antibody positivity was 13.57%, while serologically defined current syphilis (TP-ELISA and TRUST dual positivity) was 7.74%. Urine testing showed Chlamydia trachomatis 1.88% and Neisseria gonorrhoeae 1.01%; HIV antibodies 0.08%; hepatitis C virus antibodies 0.15%. Behavioral data: 30.4% reported sex with female sex workers, 21.0% with casual partners, 1.1% anal sex with male partners in prior three months. HIV testing in the past year occurred in 22.2%; only 22.4% would notify partners if infected. Multivariable models: current syphilis higher with prior STI (aOR 3.02) and prior HIV testing (aOR 1.97); younger age protective. CT and NG co-infection strongly linked (CT with NG aOR 10.51; NG with CT co-infection aOR 8.88). Calls for integrated screening, partner notification, and enhanced surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Maioria dos diagnósticos de Covid-19 em MG ocorre em crianças de até 9 anos e idosos acima de 80
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Most COVID-19 diagnoses in Minas Gerais occur in children up to 9 years old and seniors over 80.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Minas Gerais, Brazil, shows 12,299 confirmed cases from January 1 to November 19, 2026, with children aged 1–9 and adults over 80 accounting for the majority of diagnoses, and a concentration of fatalities among the elderly with comorbidities such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and chronic lung disease. The 2026 total marks a 68% drop from 2025 (38,500 cases), but SES-MG warns of potential renewed virus circulation, especially during seasonal peaks and possible El Niño effects, with October–November noting more mild-to-moderate influenza-like illness related to COVID-19 in several cities, including the Belo Horizonte Metropolitan Region. No corresponding rise in severe cases, hospitalizations, or deaths has been observed. Vaccination efforts gained momentum after ~300,000 doses arrived on November 16, with ~290,000 more expected; 768,000 doses were administered Jan–Sept 2026. Vaccination regimens include three doses for children 6 months–5 years; one dose per pregnancy for pregnant women; a dose every six months for seniors >60 and immunocompromised; annual boosters for Indigenous, quilombola, and health workers.

article.articleHeadline: Congo. Sylvain viu 46 familiares morrer de Ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo. Sylvain saw 46 relatives die from Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo near the Uganda border, with no approved vaccine or treatment. Since May this year, the outbreak has caused more than 5,000 deaths and roughly 400–500 new cases weekly, with Bunia among areas where new infections are reportedly declining. The Bundibugyo strain is associated with about 50% mortality according to the WHO. Displacement exceeds one million, hindering response due to insecurity and distrust in authorities. Transmission remains driven by close family contact and traditional funeral practices. In six months, 44-year-old Sylvain Kabona Tibasima has witnessed 46 relatives die; his infant niece Birungi died, and his sister followed a week after her daughter’s birth. Children account for more than a third of fatalities. Health workers have faced over 80 attacks at treatment centers; vaccines and therapies are still in clinical trials, with none approved.

article.articleHeadline: Santa Catarina registra baixa prevalência de tuberculose bovina e tem mais de 3 mil propriedades certificadas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Santa Catarina records low prevalence of bovine tuberculosis and has more than 3,000 certified properties.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-20, Santa Catarina, Brazil, reports bovine tuberculosis in 0.5% of rural properties, five per thousand; the herd health classification is A, among the lowest in the country. The disease is caused by Mycobacterium bovis and can pose a human health risk via direct contact with infected cattle or consumption of unpasteurized milk and dairy products. Milk and meat undergo controls: milk suppliers must present tests of all cattle aged 42 days or older at least once every 36 months; at slaughter, carcasses and viscera are inspected and lesions suggestive of TB disqualify meat for human consumption. More than 3,000 properties are certified free of brucellosis and tuberculosis—3,177 in total—mostly voluntarily. Certification requires two consecutive negative tests (6–12 months apart) and annual renewal; mandatory for properties producing artisanal cheese with raw milk. The program relies on surveillance, investigations of epidemiological links, and re-testing to safeguard health and support trade.

article.articleHeadline: Alerta em MS: sarna humana avança pela região e Batayporã já registra 26 casos -- AconteceuMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Alert in Mato Grosso do Sul: human scabies is spreading across the region and Batayporã already records 26 cases -- AconteceuMS.
article.articleSummary: Scabies (human sarcoptic mange) is spreading in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, with cases reported in Nova Andradina, Batayporã, and Ivinhema in the Vale do Ivinhema region. In Batayporã, Mayor Germino Roz said 26 people had been diagnosed as of Thursday, November 19. In Nova Andradina, authorities suspended classes; Batayporã also halted school activities on the Consciência Negra holiday, with classes to resume Monday the 23rd. Transmission occurs mainly via prolonged skin-to-skin contact with an infested person; avoid close contact and do not share clothing, towels, or bed linens. Wash items used by the infected in hot water when possible. People living with an infected person should be evaluated and may need treatment even without symptoms. Early diagnosis and proper treatment of patients and close contacts are essential to interrupt transmission; scabies is treatable and curable with appropriate therapy.

article.articleHeadline: Estudo baiano sobre tuberculose ganha destaque em congresso mundial no Rio
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bahian Study on Tuberculosis Gains Prominence at a World Congress in Rio.
article.articleSummary: Bahian study from Hospital Especializado Octávio Mangabeira (HEOM), a leading public facility for respiratory diseases in Bahia, Brazil, with IBIT participation, was presented at the Union World Conference on Lung Health 2026 in Rio de Janeiro. Infectologist Dr. Bruno Buzo reported that patients exhibiting specific chest CT abnormalities have 3.5-fold higher odds of increased tuberculosis transmissibility. The finding, if validated, could provide hospitals with a radiologic criterion to identify TB patients who require respiratory isolation and to stratify isolation needs. The conference, the world's largest gathering on pulmonary health, highlighted regional insights into TB control. The study underscores imaging biomarkers as a tool for infection control planning, potentially affecting TB management in Brazil and similar settings. Date: 2026-11-20.

article.articleHeadline: Thailand Achieved Steep Tuberculosis Reductions Across Decade Despite
article.articleSummary: Thailand's twelve-year TB surveillance (2012–2023) shows substantial declines in age-standardized incidence per 100,000, yet regional heterogeneity and localized clusters persist. Thailand remains among the WHO's 30 high-burden TB countries and progresses variably toward the End TB Strategy target for 2035. Using monthly Report 506 notifications from 77 provinces and 13 health regions, including bacteriologically confirmed and clinically diagnosed TB, the study treated recurrent episodes as independent events; drug-resistance notifications were retained. Zero-count adjustments added 0.5 to numerators, with negligible impact. COVID-19 disruptions and emerging hotspots shaped trajectories. Five of thirteen regions had significant double-digit declines, notably Health Region 3 (−20.51% average annual change; 95% CI −33.00 to −13.77) and Health Region 9 (−19.42%). Joinpoint and GAM analyses yielded concordant trends, underscoring need for localized policy interventions.

article.articleHeadline: La Libertad: centros de salud de Trujillo colapsan por aumento de dengue; región supera los 15.300 casos y reporta 13 fallecidos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: La Libertad: Trujillo health centers overwhelmed by dengue surge; region surpasses 15,300 cases and reports 13 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Dengue surge in La Libertad, Peru's Trujillo region overwhelms hospitals, with 15,399 confirmed cases and 13 deaths as of 2026-11-20. Trujillo accounts for the majority of infections, followed by Virú, Chepén and Pacasmayo. Health centers, including Melvin Jones health center in Alto Trujillo, Santa Isabel district hospital in El Porvenir, and Jerusalén hospital in La Esperanza, report sustained overcrowding as patients arrive with fever, body pains, nausea, diarrhea, and skin rashes. About 55 people remain hospitalized. Patients wait for hours in hallways and even under sun exposure due to a lack of beds and spaces not suited for care. The situation reflects a regional health emergency with ongoing dengue transmission, underscoring strained services in the district-level facilities.

article.articleHeadline: പക്ഷിപ്പനി പ്രതിരോധം: പ്രഭവ കേന്ദ്രങ്ങളുടെ പരിധിയില്‍ അണുനശീകരണം നടത്തി
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Avian Influenza Prevention: Disinfection Carried Out Within Hatchery Premises.
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza prevention in Alappuzha district, Kerala, within 1 km of outbreak centers in the Cherthala-Tripunithura gram panchayats. Four rapid-response teams in PPE disinfected poultry premises using flame gas and sodium hypochlorite spray, marking the first phase of outbreak control. Samples will be collected from a 10-km surveillance zone around the outbreak centers and biweekly sent for three months to the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal for laboratory confirmation. If all samples test negative over the three-month period, the area will be declared avian influenza-free.

article.articleHeadline: தஞ்சாவூா் மாவட்டத்தில் நாளை போலியோ சொட்டு மருந்து முகாம்
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Polio vaccination campaign in Thanjavur district tomorrow.
article.articleSummary: Polio vaccination campaign in Thanjavur district on Sunday will deliver polio drops to about 180,000 children under five. The district administration states that 1,609 vaccination centers have been set up, including 126 urban centers and 1,483 rural centers. A workforce of 6,436 vaccinators and 217 supervisors will operate. Outreach sites span primary and sub-health centers, schools, government and private hospitals, bus stands, railway stations, temples, mosques, check posts, and other public gathering places. Seventy-seven mobile vaccination teams will reach long-distance areas and migrants. Children born on November 22 must receive an additional dose during this campaign, even if they have previously received polio vaccines. Children temporarily residing in the district from other states and union territories will also be immunized.

article.articleSummary: Polio drops vaccination camps will be held at 128 locations in Tirunelveli city tomorrow, 21 November 2026, across four zones—Palayamkottai, Thachanalloor, Melapalayam, and Tirunelveli. Tirunelveli Municipal Commissioner K. Priya announced camps to provide oral polio drops to all children aged up to 5 years. In total, 37,195 children will be vaccinated. The sites include 122 permanent locations such as bus stands, the railway station, government primary health centers, NGO welfare centers, and schools; six additional high-traffic venues comprise the remaining camps. The drive aims to sustain polio immunity in the city. The article does not provide details on outbreaks, laboratory confirmation, infection sources, or imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: ISPA Menurun, Dinkes Kalsel Ingatkan Ancaman DBD Saat Musim Hujan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Acute Respiratory Infections Decline, South Kalimantan Health Office Warns of Dengue Fever Threat During the Rainy Season
article.articleSummary: South Kalimantan's Health Office (Dinkes Kalsel) warns of dengue fever risk as the rainy season begins, with standing water in containers potentially hosting Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. Although no dengue cases have risen in the province, officials urge vigilance and reinforce prevention. Head Diauddin notes stagnant water in unused containers can become breeding grounds, and the health office is launching school environmental-cleanup programs to remove such water-holding items. At the same time, health facilities in South Kalimantan are being prepared to handle possible case increases. Separately, Acute Respiratory Infections (ARIs) in Kalsel are declining as forest fires ease: weekly ARI cases previously ran 8,000–11,000 during karhutla, now about 4,000–5,000 per week. ARIs remain possible during the rainy season but are not as severe as during smoky periods. Public health messages emphasize hygiene and mosquito control around homes.

article.articleHeadline: 45 students hospitalised for food poisoning at UoH
article.articleSummary: Around 45 students at Hyderabad Central University (HCU) in Gachibowli, Hyderabad, were admitted to the University Primary Health Centre on Friday with suspected food poisoning after dinner on Thursday night. The incident affected residents of New Research Scholars (NRS) and M-Hostel, two boys’ hostels at the University of Hyderabad (UoH); a few students sought treatment outside campus. Unions said the patients were stable but not fully recovered. Food prepared at the NRS hostel was transported to M-Hostels due to the latter lacking a separate kitchen, with meals prepared by staff under a kitchen supervisor. The Dean of Students’ Welfare visited the health centre to review treatment. Students demanded a nutritionist, better maintenance of hostel messes, improved medical care, and relaxation for students during examinations.

article.articleHeadline: الولايات المتحدة تفرض قيودا على السفر جوا للحد من انتقال إيبولا من...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United States imposes air travel restrictions to curb the spread of Ebola from ...
article.articleSummary: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention impose new air travel safeguards to curb the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Effective Nov 3, all international travelers to the United States must sign a declaration that they were not in the DRC in the prior 21 days. Travelers and flight crews who visited the DRC within the last three weeks are not allowed to board US-bound international flights, including U.S. citizens. The outbreak, caused by Ebola virus, Bundibugyo strain, is the second-largest on record and spreading faster than previous waves. As of Nov 8, Congo's confirmed cases reached about 11,000 with roughly 5,400 deaths. Secondary cases have been linked in France, Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, but the United States reports no linked infections and overall national risk remains low. The measures aim to reduce importation risk while authorities monitor the situation.

triage.headline_ja: 米国、コンゴ民主共和国からのエボラ出血熱拡散を抑制するため航空渡航制限を導入
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去2番目の規模のエボラ流行（約11,000例、死亡約5,400人）が発生し、複数国へ二次感染が確認され、米国が渡航制限を導入するなどIHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するため。
triage.notes: 発生地域にUnited States、France、Kenya、Uganda、Nigeriaが含まれるが、これらは二次感染・渡航制限の文脈であり主発生地はDRCのみ。対象国リストにはDRCのみ含まれるため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية بدأت كل من كينيا ونيجيريا عدًّا تنازليًا لمدة 42 يومًا لإعلان انتهاء تفشي إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The World Health Organization has begun a 42-day countdown for Kenya and Nigeria to declare the end of the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization has begun a 42-day countdown for Kenya and Nigeria to declare the end of the Ebola outbreak. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the latest update (as of 17 November 2026, following a report on 6 November 2026) shows ongoing transmission with 11,613 confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths (case fatality rate 48.9%). The outbreak spans 68 health zones across 8 provinces, with active transmission in 48 zones. Ituri and North Kivu remain the hardest-hit provinces; South Kivu and South Ubangi have not reported a case for more than 42 days. A high proportion of deaths occur in communities outside treatment centers, especially among young children, underscoring challenges in early detection and access to care.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関（WHO）、ケニアとナイジェリアでエボラ流行終息宣言に向けた42日間のカウントダウンを開始
triage.triage_reason: DRCで11,613例・死亡5,678例（致死率48.9%）と大規模な継続的流行があり、68保健地区中48地区で活動的感染が続いている。公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクがあり、IHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリアは終息に向けた42日カウントダウンの対象であり、対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCでのエボラ流行は依然として進行中で致死率が高く、早期発見・医療アクセスの課題が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Paciente com mpox relata despreparo em unidade de saúde no Ceará
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Patient with mpox reports lack of preparedness at a health facility in Ceará.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (MPXV, Orthopoxvirus) cases are rising in Ceará, Brazil, with 175 confirmed infections in the year and 145 in Fortaleza. A 30-year-old Fortaleza videomaker reported lack of preparedness at a UPA emergency unit, prompting him to seek care at Hospital São José, a regional infectious-disease center. He first experienced influenza-like symptoms in early November—fever, body aches, sore throat—before skin lesions appeared four days later. Most cases involve men aged 24–51. Caucaia, in the metropolitan region, rose from one to seven cases within a week, while Sobral has four. Authorities, via the Sesa epidemiological coordinator Ana Cabral, note mpox is transmitted mainly through direct contact with skin lesions, mucous membranes, or secretions, and that illness typically lasts 2–4 weeks and is usually mild to moderate.

triage.headline_ja: セアラ州の医療機関で準備不足を訴えるmpox患者
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・セアラ州でmpox症例が急増（週内に1→7例など）しており、医療現場の対応不足や地域拡大、社会的関心（患者の訴え・行政コメント）が確認されるため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 症例は軽症〜中等症が中心で死亡例の記載はないが、特定地域（Caucaia）で短期間に症例が急増しており、地域保健当局が公式にコメントしている点から継続監視・評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: کشف ویژگی‌های تازه گونه نادر ایبولا در کنگو؛ مرگ ۷۰ درصد کودکان مبتلا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Discovery of new features of a rare Ebola strain in the Congo; 70% mortality among infected children.
article.articleSummary: Rare Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 5,500 people and infected over 11,000 since its April emergence, six months into the crisis. The spread is nearly twice as fast as the 2013–2015 West Africa outbreak. Bleeding occurs in only 5–10% of Bundibugyo cases, contradicting common Ebola expectations, and early diagnostics often miss Bundibugyo because assays target other Ebola species. About 70% of patients die outside treatment centers. Children under five (1,207 cases) suffer a 70% fatality (844 deaths); adults’ fatality rate around 50%. Gastrointestinal symptoms predominate in children, complicating rapid diagnosis and care. Genomic analyses show Bundibugyo does not rapidly mutate nor increase transmissibility. No approved vaccine or therapy exists for Bundibugyo. Trials include Merck's Ervebo for Zaire ebolavirus and Bundibugyo-specific vaccines, plus antivirals from Gilead Sciences and Map Biopharmaceuticals. Researchers hope these efforts help contain the second-largest Ebola outbreak in history.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴにおける希少エボラ株の新たな特徴の発見；感染した子供の70%が死亡
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのブンディブギョ・エボラウイルス大流行は感染者1万人超、死者5500人超と規模が大きく、ワクチン・治療法未承認かつ拡大速度が速いため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生イベントである。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリー上では言及がなく、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外した。史上2番目の規模とされる大規模アウトブレイクであり、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Indore To Get Yellow Fever Vaccination Centre At MY Hospital From November 27, No More Trips To AIIMS Bhopal
article.articleSummary: Yellow fever vaccination centre will open at Maharaja Yeshwantrao Hospital (MYH), Indore, on November 27, 2026, after Central Government approval. MGM Medical College and MYH obtained clearance following a two-year process that began with an October inspection by the Regional Director of the Health Ministry; the Central International Health Division approved subsequently. The service returns to Indore after being suspended during the Covid era; previously Government Hukumchand Hospital offered vaccination, and AIIMS Bhopal has been the sole centre in Madhya Pradesh since. Last year AIIMS Bhopal experienced vaccine shortages lasting about two to three months, creating travel difficulties for international travellers; roughly 200–250 vaccinations are administered monthly there, including residents of the Indore division. Yellow fever is a viral disease with fever and headache and can cause bleeding and organ involvement; vaccination is mandatory for travellers to many African and South American destinations (more than 40 countries) for those aged nine months and above.

triage.headline_ja: インドール市、11月27日よりMY病院に黄熱病ワクチン接種センター開設、AIIMS Bhopalへの往来不要に
triage.triage_reason: 黄熱病の発生報告ではなく、渡航者向けワクチン接種センター開設という行政サービスに関する記事であり、公衆衛生上の異常事態や感染拡大のリスクは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Nanopartículas de prata se mostraram eficazes contra o Aedes aegypti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Silver nanoparticles proved effective against Aedes aegypti
article.articleSummary: Green-synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) show high efficacy against Aedes aegypti larvae and schistosome cercariae in water. In a Butantan Institute study led by Luiz Gustavo Ribeiro and Ana Olivia de Souza, AgNPs produced via fungal extracts from Aspergillus tubingensis (isolated from a mangrove) kill Schistosoma cercariae at low concentrations within two hours, preventing transmission from contaminated rivers and lakes. The same nanoparticles blocked the progression of Aedes aegypti larvae to adults 48 hours after application, reducing dengue, Zika, and chikungunya risk. Unlike chemical molluscicides, the approach does not kill snails, fish, or microcrustaceans in tested conditions, due to gradual release. Patented by INPI in July 2026, the technology is ready for industrial scaling and licensing. Dengue affects up to 400 million annually (WHO); Brazil logged over 1 million cases in 2025 and 6.6 million in 2024, while schistosomiasis affects over 200 million globally and remains endemic in parts of Brazil.

triage.headline_ja: 銀ナノ粒子がネッタイシマカに対して効果を示した
triage.triage_reason: 研究開発・技術革新に関する記事であり、疾病の発生や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報告するものではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事はブタンタン研究所による蚊幼虫・住血吸虫セルカリアに対する銀ナノ粒子の防除技術開発に関する科学・技術ニュースであり、具体的な疾病アウトブレイクの報告ではない。デング熱等の既存の背景統計は参考情報として記載されているのみ。

article.articleHeadline: Century of Newcastle Disease Virus Research Traces Evolution and Vaccine
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) is a notifiable avian pathogen (Paramyxoviridae, Avulavirinae, Orthoavulavirus javaense) with economic impact from high flock mortality, reduced egg production, and trade embargoes. A centennial retrospective traces its identification in 1926 after outbreaks in Java, Indonesia and Newcastle-upon-Tyne, England. NDV comprises Class II genotypes and a Class I lineage; genomes are about 15.2 kb. The virion carries HN and F glycoproteins; V and W proteins arise via translational frameshifts and antagonize host interferon signaling (STAT1, MDA5). Infection starts with HN binding sialic acids and a pH-independent F protein fusion after proteolytic cleavage. Pathotypes span viscerotropic velogenic (up to 100% mortality in naive birds within 3–9 days), neurotropic velogenic, and mesogenic forms. US eradication efforts (1971–73, 2002–03) depopulated millions of birds and cost hundreds of millions. Since the 1920s, NDV has caused at least four major panzootics with persistent endemicity in wildlife and poultry.

triage.headline_ja: ニューカッスル病ウイルス研究100年の歩み：進化とワクチンの課題
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はニューカッスル病ウイルスに関する歴史的・学術的レビューであり、現在進行中の新規アウトブレイクの報告ではないため、トリアージ対象としない。
triage.notes: 記事は1926年の発見から現在までのNDVの研究史・ワクチン開発の総説であり、特定の現在進行中の発生国に関する報告ではない。インドネシア・英国・米国は歴史的発生地として言及されているのみで、現時点のアウトブレイクを示すものではないためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Pemprov Papua Pegunungan perkuat penanganan penyakit ATM
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Papua Highlands Provincial Government Strengthens Management of Acute Transverse Myelitis.
article.articleSummary: On 21 November 2026, the Papua Highlands Provincial Government, via the Health Office in Wamena, strengthened management of AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria (ATM) in the region. Four strategic steps guide the effort: data-driven policy based on the latest surveillance or real-time data; cross-sector integration; strengthening the regional partnership forum; and concrete actions in six focus districts. Programs must be aligned with real-time data to ensure targeted interventions and be incorporated into RPJMD, RKPD, and APBD at provincial and district levels. The initiative also emphasizes a strengthened forum for government, partners, academia, business, and civil society to coordinate efforts. The six districts designated as ATM loci are Jayawijaya, Mamberamo Tengah, Nduga, Pegunungan Bintang, Yalimo, and Yahukimo. An integrated ATM action plan for these districts should be drafted and implemented promptly.

triage.headline_ja: パプア高地州政府、AIDS・結核・マラリア（ATM）対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: 既知の風土病（AIDS・結核・マラリア）に対する行政の施策強化に関する記事であり、新規の異常事態や急性の公衆衛生リスクを示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は既存の風土病対策プログラムの行政的強化を報じるものであり、新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Waspada DBD dan Banjir
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Beware Dengue Fever and Floods.
article.articleSummary: In South Kalimantan, heavier rains raise dengue fever risk and flood hazards as the rainy season arrives. While acute respiratory infection (ISPA) cases, previously spiking due to forest fires, have fallen from about 8,000–11,000 per week to 4,000–5,000 per week, health authorities warn that threats persist. Standing water around homes, schools, and communities fosters Aedes aegypti breeding; discarded containers, cans, buckets, and other debris serve as reservoirs. Dengue prevention must begin now with expanded vector-control campaigns beyond schools to involve families, RTs, villages, and urban villages, turning avoidance into a shared habit. Flood risk persists in Banjarmasin and Banjarbaru due to drainage issues; river normalization and drainage cleaning are underway, but benefits must reach residents. Emergency preparedness, including effective early warning systems, rapid information flow via desa and volunteers, is essential. Local residents, such as Pengaron in Paramasan, provide valuable water-condition monitoring.

triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング熱・洪水注意喚起に関する一般的な公衆衛生啓発記事であり、異常な増加や重症例の急増等の具体的報告はなく、基準に該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: 'A variante parece ter maior transmissibilidade', diz infectologista sobre alta da covid-19
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 'The variant seems to have greater transmissibility,' says an infectious disease specialist about the rise in COVID-19 cases.
article.articleSummary: Stratus (XFG), a SARS-CoV-2 variant descended from Omicron, is driving renewed COVID-19 transmission in Brazil, representing about 90% of samples in Ministry of Health genomic surveillance. Seventeen states and the Federal District report significant case growth; test positivity rose 1% to 17% over three months, the year’s high. Fiocruz notes increased hospitalizations for COVID-19–related severe acute respiratory syndrome. Experts attribute the surge to higher transmissibility and climate factors, with São Paulo’s rainy, cooler days promoting indoor spread. A study found Stratus does not cause more severe disease or immune escape. As of November 9, 2026, Brazil recorded 118,920 cases, 3,641 severe, and 445 deaths, lower than pandemic peaks. Vaccination remains the main protection, especially for older adults (68% of deaths were ≥65); boosters are advised for those never vaccinated or at high risk.

triage.headline_ja: 「この変異株はより高い感染力を持つようだ」と感染症専門医がCOVID-19の増加について語る
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19新変異株（Stratus/XFG）によるブラジル国内の感染再拡大が報告されているが、重症化や免疫逃避の増加はないとされ、死亡数もパンデミックピークを下回っており、国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急性は低いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 新変異株Stratus(XFG)はオミクロン系統で、重症化や免疫逃避の増加は確認されていない。ブラジル国内17州で症例増加が報告されているが、死亡数・重症例数はパンデミックピークより低水準。
